title: 关于开展零碳园区建设的通知
source: 国家发展改革委等3部门
summary: 发改环资〔2025〕910号。部署开展零碳园区建设，明确建设目标、重点任务与申报要求，推动园区绿色低碳转型示范。
_ev: ti:关于开展零碳园区建设的通知
content:
关于开展零碳园区建设的通知(发改环资〔2025〕910号)
国家发展改革委 工业和信息化部 国家能源局关于开展零碳园区建设的通知 发改环资〔2025〕910号
各省、自治区、直辖市发展改革委、工业和信息化主管部门、能源局：
为贯彻落实党中央、国务院决策部署，积极稳妥推进碳达峰碳中和，加快经济社会发展全面绿色转型，支持有条件的地区率先建成一批零碳园区，逐步完善相关规划设计、技术装备、商业模式和管理规范，有计划、分步骤推进各类园区低碳化零碳化改造，助力园区和企业减碳增效，为实现碳达峰碳中和目标提供坚实有力支撑。现就零碳园区建设有关事项通知如下：
一、重点任务
（一）加快园区用能结构转型。加强园区及周边可再生能源开发利用，支持园区与周边非化石能源发电资源匹配对接，科学配置储能等调节性资源，因地制宜发展绿电直连、新能源就近接入增量配电网等绿色电力直接供应模式，鼓励参与绿证绿电交易，探索氢电耦合开发利用模式。推动园区积极利用生物质能、核能、光热、地热、工业余热等热能资源，实现供热系统清洁低碳化。探索氢能、生物质等替代化石燃料和原料。
（二）大力推进园区节能降碳。推动园区建立用能和碳排放管理制度，深入推进企业能效碳效诊断评估，加强重点用能设备节能监察和日常监管，淘汰落后产能、落后工艺、落后产品设备。支持企业对标标杆水平和先进水平，实施节能降碳改造和用能设备更新，鼓励企业建设极致能效工厂、零碳工厂。
（三）调整优化园区产业结构。鼓励园区加快自身产业结构优化调整，布局发展低能耗、低污染、高附加值的新兴产业，探索以绿色能源制造绿色产品的“以绿制绿”模式。支持高载能产业有序向资源可支撑、能源有保障、环境有容量的园区转移集聚，探索深度降碳路径。
（四）强化园区资源节约集约。统筹规划园区及企业空间布局，提高土地资源集约利用水平，促进能量梯级利用、水资源循环利用。健全园区废弃物循环利用网络，推进工业固体废弃物、余压余热余冷、废气废液废渣资源化利用。
（五）完善升级园区基础设施。优化园区基础设施规划设计，系统推进电力、热力、燃气、氢能、供排水、污染治理等基础设施的建设改造。推动新建建筑按照超低能耗建筑、近零能耗建筑标准设计建造。完善园区绿色交通基础设施，加快运输工具低碳零碳替代。
（六）加强先进适用技术应用。支持园区与企业、高校、科研机构开展深度合作，加强科技成果转化应用，探索绿色低碳技术研发与产业发展深度融合机制，围绕低碳零碳负碳先进适用技术打造示范应用场景，形成具有商业价值的技术解决方案。
（七）提升园区能碳管理能力。支持园区建设覆盖主要用能企业的能碳管理平台，强化园区及企业用能负荷监控、预测与调配能力，为碳排放核算、源网匹配调节、电力需求侧管理、多能协同互补、资源高效循环利用等工作提供支撑。
（八）支持园区加强改革创新。支持地方政府、园区企业、发电企业、电网企业、能源综合服务商等各类主体参与零碳园区建设，围绕实现高比例可再生能源供给消纳探索路径模式。鼓励有条件的园区以虚拟电厂（负荷聚合商）等形式参与电力市场，提高资源配置效率和电力系统稳定性。
二、保障措施
国家发展改革委将统筹利用现有资金渠道支持零碳园区建设，鼓励各地区对零碳园区建设给予资金支持，通过地方政府专项债券资金等支持符合条件的项目。鼓励政策性银行对符合条件的项目给予中长期信贷支持。支持符合条件的企业发行债券用于零碳园区建设。支持园区引入外部人才、技术和专业机构，服务企业节能降碳改造、碳排放核算管理、产品碳足迹认证等。探索对零碳园区多能互补、多能联供项目实行“一个窗口”审批制度。强化用能要素保障，在零碳园区范围内创新节能审查和碳排放评价模式，探索实施区域审批或项目备案。加强新建园区、新能源电源、供电设施等用地用海要素保障。
三、组织实施
（一）加强统筹协调。国家发展改革委统筹推进零碳园区建设，持续深化相关领域改革创新，在试点探索、项目建设、资金安排等方面对零碳园区建设给予积极支持。工业和信息化部指导各地区推进工业园区低碳化改造，推动具备条件的工业园区建设零碳园区。国家能源局指导各地区加强零碳园区绿色能源供给体系建设和改革创新，推动园区供用能模式变革。各地区发展改革委要会同本地区工业和信息化、能源主管部门等结合实际抓好工作落实。
（二）组织园区申报。在综合考虑能源禀赋、产业基础、电力安全可靠供应、减碳潜力等因素基础上，各地区发展改革委要会同本地区工业和信息化、能源主管部门等推荐有条件、有意愿的园区建设国家级零碳园区（基本条件见附件1），并指导园区综合分析项目可行性，测算经济、环境、社会效益，按要求编制申报书（大纲见附件2）。各地区推荐园区数量不超过2个，于8月22日前将推荐园区名单及建设方案报送国家发展改革委（环资司）。
（三）扎实开展建设。国家发展改革委会同有关方面对地方推荐园区的建设方案进行审核，统筹考虑产业代表性、综合示范性、碳减排潜力等因素，确定首批国家级零碳园区建设名单。对于纳入建设名单的园区，各地区发展改革委要加强工作指导，协调解决困难问题。各地区可结合实际开展省级零碳园区建设。
（四）加强评估总结。国家级零碳园区建设期满后，由省级发展改革委组织开展自评估。自评估符合要求的，由国家发展改革委组织有关部门和单位开展评估验收（指标体系见附件3），通过评估验收的园区正式成为国家级零碳园区。各地区发展改革委要会同有关方面及时掌握本地区零碳园区建设进展，梳理总结经验，为相关行业、区域和其他园区低碳化改造探索有益经验。

title: 光伏能耗能效国标发布 筑牢光伏产业绿色发展底线
source: 工业和信息化部（央视新闻）
summary: 工信部联合发改委、市场监管总局发布三项光伏领域强制性国家标准，覆盖硅料、硅片、组件、逆变器全链条，划定能耗能效刚性约束。
content: 工信部联合发改委、市场监管总局发布《硅单晶单位产品能源消耗限额》《晶体硅光伏组件和逆变器能效限定值及能效等级》《硅多晶和锗单位产品能源消耗限额》三项光伏领域强制性国家标准，覆盖多晶硅、硅片、组件、逆变器全链条，分等级设定能耗能效指标，严控高耗能低效产能；组件创新纳入耦合环境应力衰减率评价指标。三项标准系统衔接，统一全链条能耗能效核算规则，提高光伏产品绿色准入门槛，促进光伏产业转型升级，支撑能源绿色低碳转型与“双碳”目标落地。

title: 生态环境部：我国已成为全球规模最大的碳市场
summary: 全国碳市场上线5周年，累计成交量突破9.17亿吨、成交额超617亿元；2026年上半年成交量同比增约37%，覆盖排放量占全国65%以上。
content: 7月16日是全国碳排放权交易市场上线交易5周年。截至2026年6月，全国碳市场配额累计成交量突破9.17亿吨、成交额超617亿元；2026年上半年成交量5296万吨、同比增长约37%。纳入重点排放单位由最初2162家火电企业扩容至3378家（钢铁、水泥、铝冶炼等高耗能企业），覆盖约83亿吨CO2、占全国排放总量65%以上。“十四五”期间仅火电行业通过碳市场实现5.3亿吨实打实碳减排，约80%企业碳排放强度下降，协同减排二氧化硫2.7万吨、氮氧化物9.4万吨、烟尘13.5万吨。生态环境部明确到2027年实现工业领域重点排放行业全覆盖，让碳价体现减排成本，支撑“十五五”全国碳市场覆盖行业单位产品碳排放下降3%目标。
_ev: ti:生态环境部 我国已成为全球规模最大的

title: 锚定2030碳达峰目标 银行“三箭齐发”服务绿色转型
summary: 商业银行围绕“十五五”碳达峰加快布局碳金融，从交易结算、投融资、投行咨询三方向激活碳资产价值，助力高碳行业有序转型。
content: 商业银行围绕国务院《“十五五”碳达峰行动方案》加快布局绿色转型业务，工商银行绿色金融课题组提出碳金融服务生态“三箭齐发”：一是做优交易结算（账户开立、资金存管清算、履约保障、跨境结算）；二是做强投融资，以碳配额、CCER、碳汇预期收益权等环境权益为抓手精准滴灌实体经济；三是做深投行咨询（转型路径规划、碳资产估值、碳风险管理）。大行主攻国家级绿色基建与高碳行业转型融资及碳核算平台建设，中小行深耕本地分布式光伏、工商业储能、节能改造、园区循环经济等小微场景。业内提示碳市场2027年起对新纳入行业配额逐步收紧、信息披露趋严，须将企业排放强度与碳成本纳入授信决策，防范高碳资产重定价信用风险。

title: 欧盟绿色合规进入“真金白银”时代：上市公司供应链数据安全与订单保卫战
summary: 欧盟CBAM 2026年起实质收费、DPP注册系统7月投运，覆盖多行业中国出口企业，数据合规与商业机密保护成核心挑战。
content: 2026年1月1日欧盟碳边境调节机制（CBAM）正式进入实质收费阶段，进口商自2027年起购买CBAM证书覆盖2026年排放；数字产品护照（DPP）注册系统已于2026年7月投运，电池2027年2月18日起强制、2030年扩至多数消费品。CBAM首批覆盖钢铁、铝、水泥、化肥、电力、氢六大行业303个海关税号，2028年大幅扩围新增约180种钢铝下游产品，预计新增受影响中国企业7000—8000家。惩罚机制上，使用默认值将被加征额外系数：2026年10%、2027年20%、2028年30%；数据责任沿供应链传导至中国工厂，企业面临“交数据怕泄密、不交数据成本高”的两难，电子企业对欧合规率不足40%。

title: 我国首个全链条绿色低碳乙烯工程投产 零碳园区建设获石化范本
summary: 独山子石化塔里木120万吨乙烯绿色低碳示范工程投产，建成全球首个乙烯裂解炉烟气碳循环利用示范基地；同期发布水风光一体化大模型及碳足迹等14项国标。
content: 7月16日中石油独山子石化塔里木120万吨/年二期乙烯及配套绿色低碳示范工程正式投产，位于新疆库尔勒上库工业园区（全国首批国家级零碳园区中唯一以高耗能石化产业为主的园区），总投资256.56亿元，建成全球首个乙烯裂解炉烟气碳循环利用示范基地，为零碳园区提供石化工业绿色低碳范本。同日我国发布首个面向千万千瓦级水风光一体化清洁能源基地的智慧运营大模型（四川），融合AI与大数据贯通预测预报、电力调度、生产运行等场景；市场监管总局（国家标准委）批准发布508项重要国家标准，其中节能环保方面发布碳足迹等14项国家标准、钢筋和不锈钢绿色产品评价等45项，推动绿色低碳产业规范发展。

title: 南通以零碳试点建设竞逐绿色新赛道
source: 南通市人民政府（南通日报）
summary: 南通首批25家（近）零碳试点全面铺开，目标建成超100个微电网项目，布局零碳认证、绿电认证、碳资产管理服务体系，并加入国际零碳零废城市发展联盟。
content:
一年多来，我市首批25家试点全面铺开并取得阶段性突破——
以零碳试点建设竞逐绿色新赛道
字体：[ 大 中 小 ]
盛夏时节，走进海门港新区中天钢铁集团（南通）有限公司，厂房屋顶的光伏板在阳光下熠熠生辉，这片整齐排布的光伏矩阵，是全省最大的屋顶分布式光伏发电项目。
“废水实现全部循环回用，工业固废几乎做到‘吃干榨净’，就连生产过程中产生的余热，也能转化为清洁能源。”中天钢铁南通公司相关负责人介绍，作为南通市首批（近）零碳制造业工厂，企业已累计投入近百亿元用于绿色低碳发展，以实际行动重新定义“钢铁是怎样炼成的”。而这，只是南通追“新”逐“绿”的一个缩影。
向“绿”而行：厚植发展新优势
86公里绵长的海岸线，不仅是风景，更是如东零碳建设的“能量源泉”。全省唯一汇集风电、光伏、储能、工业用户所有要素的变电站——220千伏绿电专变（双南变）就建在如东沿海经济开发区（洋口镇）。它像一位精准的“调度员”，将各种清洁能源通过专属绿电专线，“点对点”送进企业车间。“每一度电来自何方，碳排放是多少，都能像快递单号一样全程追溯。”国网南通供电公司相关负责人打了个形象的比喻。
这一模式具有重要示范意义。目前，如东洋口港、启东吕四港、通州湾示范经济开发区等多家产业园区正加快绿电专线、专变建设，推动绿电就地就近消纳、可物理溯源。预计到“十五五”末，接入园区新能源规模超700万千瓦，年提供可溯源绿电超160亿千瓦·时，园区可实现绿电占比80%以上。与此同时，如皋、如东、启东三地已完成国家整县屋顶分布式光伏开发试点。
2024年10月，《南通市（近）零碳试点建设实施方案》正式印发，共选取5个产业园区、12个制造业工厂、5个“数智化”微电网、3个虚拟电厂开展试点建设。为激发不同主体的主动性和创造性，推动各项试点任务顺利完成，我市在全省率先出台《南通市（近）零碳试点奖补政策实施细则》。这场“零碳”行动，远不止于生态情怀，更是南通落实“向海图强”战略、抢占绿色发展制高点的关键落子，为城市高质量发展注入强劲动能。
厚积以成势：交出亮眼“成绩单”
一年多来，在市发改委统筹推进、各试点单位协同发力下，南通交出了一份亮眼的“成绩单”，各领域试点均取得阶段性突破——
在产业园区层面，如东洋口港开发区、启东吕四港开发区成功纳入首批省级碳达峰碳中和试点园区，成为全省园区低碳转型的标杆；如东能楹100MWh重力储能示范项目，入选国家能源领域首台（套）重大技术装备，同时被纳入国家绿色低碳先进技术示范项目清单。
全市共3个项目入选该清单，数量居全省第一。此外，由苏州、南通、盐城共同申报的“江苏沿江滨海氢能产业创新协同发展试点”，成功入选国家能源局首批能源领域氢能试点名单。三地正按照“一体、三核、多团组”的总体思路，着力推动氢能“制储输用”全链条发展，加速形成可复制、可推广的产业发展模式。
在制造业工厂领域，中天钢铁、中远船务跻身首批省级碳达峰碳中和试点企业，分别围绕行业能效标杆和低碳供应链开展试点，推动传统重工业向绿色化、高端化转型；百年老厂大生集团，将数字化、智能化、物联网与绿色低碳技术深度融合，建成中纺联认证的国内首个碳中和智慧纺纱工厂，让传统纺织业焕发新生。
在“数智化”微电网领域，3个试点已接入市级能碳管理平台，实现源网荷储实时监测和协调控制。其中，中天科技微电网试点构建了以“分布式光伏+储能+充电桩+工业柔性负荷”为核心的微电网系统，年自发自用电量约2700万千瓦·时，仅电费一项就节约730万元，既实现了绿色降碳，又为企业带来了实实在在的经济效益。
虚拟电厂同样跑出“加速度”。国电投虚拟电厂试点已聚合用户20家，总容量244兆瓦，可调容量70兆瓦，多次响应省调度中心辅助服务指令，在用电高峰时像“充电宝联盟”一样统一调度，既保安全又创效益。
向未来发力：构建发展新生态

从沿江到沿海，从工厂车间到产业园区，一场向“绿”而行的变革正在南通全面铺开。向海图强，不仅是向海洋要空间、要产业，更是要一份面向未来的、可持续的“绿色答案”。而这，正是南通迈向“下一个万亿”的坚实底气。

全市共3个项目入选该清单，数量居全省第一。此外，由苏州、南通、盐城共同申报的“江苏沿江滨海氢能产业创新协同发展试点”，成功入选国家能源局首批能源领域氢能试点名单。三地正按照“一体、三核、多团组”的总体思路，着力推动氢能“制储输用”全链条发展，加速形成可复制、可推广的产业发展模式。
在制造业工厂领域，中天钢铁、中远船务跻身首批省级碳达峰碳中和试点企业，分别围绕行业能效标杆和低碳供应链开展试点，推动传统重工业向绿色化、高端化转型；百年老厂大生集团，将数字化、智能化、物联网与绿色低碳技术深度融合，建成中纺联认证的国内首个碳中和智慧纺纱工厂，让传统纺织业焕发新生。
在“数智化”微电网领域，3个试点已接入市级能碳管理平台，实现源网荷储实时监测和协调控制。其中，中天科技微电网试点构建了以“分布式光伏+储能+充电桩+工业柔性负荷”为核心的微电网系统，年自发自用电量约2700万千瓦·时，仅电费一项就节约730万元，既实现了绿色降碳，又为企业带来了实实在在的经济效益。

title: 2026工业母机绿色制造6项核心要求落地 成刚性准入门槛
source: 工业和信息化部等五部门
summary: 在欧盟CBAM与国内《制造业绿色低碳发展行动方案》硬约束下，工业母机绿色制造成市场准入门槛；五部门《工业产品绿色设计指南（2026年版）》要求全链条降碳。
content:
2026工业母机绿色制造 6项核心要求落地 为何成为刚性准入门槛？
新浪极客前线
07.06 04:05
确定不再关注此人吗
确定取消
2026工业母机绿色制造 6项核心要求落地 为何成为刚性准入门槛？
2026年全球制造业绿色转型进入硬约束阶段，作为制造业核心装备的工业母机，绿色制造已从行业可选项变为刚性准入要求，明确了6项核心落地标准，绿色指标成为下游用户采购选型的关键决策权重[1]。
2026年7月4日，工业和信息化部装备工业发展中心在2026“工业母机+”百行万企产需对接活动上，正式发布《工业母机智能化变革十大趋势展望（2026）》，将绿色制造列为工业母机高端化、智能化转型的核心方向；此前2026年上半年，工业和信息化部联合国家发展改革委、教育部、生态环境部、市场监管总局五部门，已经联合印发《工业产品绿色设计指南（2026年版）》，明确要求包括工业母机在内的所有重点工业产品全面推行绿色设计，从源头构建全生命周期降碳体系[1][2]。
工业母机被称为“制造机器的机器”，是航空航天、汽车、新能源、半导体、工程机械等所有高端制造领域的核心基础装备，其本身的能耗、碳排放水平，直接决定了下游制造业全产业链的绿色转型成效。在我国“双碳”目标进入落地攻坚阶段的背景下，工业母机的绿色制造要求被提升至前所未有的战略高度，行业传统的“重能耗、高损耗、低循环”发展模式正在被彻底重构[3]。
为何2026年工业母机绿色制造从可选项变为必选项？
核心原因是全球制造业绿色转型的政策硬约束已经落地，绿色制造不再是行业自愿选择的加分项，而是进入市场的准入门槛[1]。
从全球范围来看，欧盟碳边境调节机制（CBAM）已经从2026年正式实施，中国出口制造业的所有终端产品都需要核算全产业链碳排放，而工业母机作为生产端的核心装备，其碳排放水平直接计入下游产品的碳足迹，如果工业母机本身不满足绿色要求，下游制造企业的产品将无法满足出口的碳核算要求，面临额外的碳关税成本。
从国内政策来看，我国《制造业绿色低碳发展行动方案（2025—2027年）》已经明确了阶段性降碳目标，要求规模以上制造业单位增加值能耗持续下降，而工业母机作为装备制造业的能耗大户，同时也是所有制造环节的源头装备，自然成为政策监管的核心对象。此次五部门联合印发的《工业产品绿色设计指南（2026年版）》，直接将工业母机列为重点推行绿色设计的产品品类，要求从设计、生产、使用到回收全链条落实绿色要求，相当于从政策层面确立了绿色制造的刚性地位[2]。
从市场端来看，下游制造企业的绿色需求已经彻底觉醒：一方面，下游企业自身需要满足双碳考核要求，自然会要求上游供应的核心装备满足绿色指标；另一方面，下游终端消费市场对绿色产品的偏好也在提升，越来越多的品牌厂商开始要求供应商提供全产业链碳足迹证明，而工业母机的碳排放数据是其中必不可少的环节。正是在政策、市场、全球贸易规则的多重驱动下，2026年工业母机的绿色制造才彻底从可选变为必须[1]。
行业机构的调研数据也印证了这一变化：据公开报道，2025年国内工业母机下游采购中，将绿色指标纳入采购标准的企业占比不足30%，而2026年上半年这一占比已经提升至超过75%，其中头部汽车、新能源、航空航天企业100%将绿色指标列为采购的必要条件，这一变化速度远超行业此前的预期。
2026年工业母机绿色制造的6项核心要求具体是什么？
根据《工业母机智能化变革十大趋势展望（2026）》和《工业产品绿色设计指南（2026年版）》的公开内容，2026年工业母机绿色制造明确了6项可落地的核心要求，覆盖从设计、生产、使用到回收的全流程[1][2]。
1. 能效自优化与资源按需供给
这一要求的核心是将智能感知与人工智能算法深度嵌入工业母机的能效管理体系，实现电能、切削液等各类生产资源的按需供给，彻底改变传统机床“重能耗、高损耗”的运行模式[1]。传统工业母机大多按照固定参数运行，即使在轻负载加工场景下，也会保持满功率输出，造成了大量的能源浪费；而搭载AI能效自优化系统的新型工业母机，可以通过传感器实时感知加工负载，AI算法动态调整加工参数和能耗输出，实现“多加工多供给、少加工少供给”，综合能耗可以降低15%-30%，优势非常明显。
2. 碳足迹追踪成为标配功能
\p>2026年新上市的工业母机，必须将碳足迹追踪作为标配功能，要求工业母机在自身全生命周期内，从原材料采购、加工制造、使用运行到最终报废回收，都具备精确的碳排放数据采集、追踪和报告能力，可以随时向下游用户提供完整的碳足迹数据，满足下游企业的碳核算需求[1]。这意味着，今后每一台工业母机都将拥有自己的“碳身份证”，所有碳排放数据可查、可追溯、可报告，彻底解决了过去碳足迹核算数据不准确、来源不可靠的问题。
3. 绿色指标成为用户选型关键权重
绿色指标已经成为下游用户采购工业母机时的关键决策权重，过去用户选型只关注精度、稳定性、加工效率等传统性能指标，现在能效等级、碳排放水平、资源利用率等绿色指标的权重，已经超过了传统指标的三分之一，部分对绿色要求高的行业，绿色指标的权重甚至超过了50%，成为决定采购结果的核心因素[1]。
4. 全生命周期的绿色设计
按照《工业产品绿色设计指南（2026年版）》要求，工业母机必须从设计阶段就考虑全生命周期的环境影响，具体分为三个核心方向：一是节能设计，要求采用节能型机床结构、轻量化机身、高效驱动系统，从源头降低基础能耗；二是绿色工艺，要求在工业母机的加工环节普及切削液循环利用、干式切削、低温加工等绿色工艺，减少耗材消耗和污染物排放；三是模块化可拆解设计，方便后期的维修、部件更换和回收再利用[2][3]。
5. 从设备到系统的协同绿色制造
工业母机的绿色制造不再局限于单台设备的节能降碳，而是拓展到“工业母机+机器人+辅助装备”一体化协同系统，通过群体智能技术构筑全工艺链协同制造新体系，实现整条产线的能效最优，而不是单台设备的最优[1]。过去很多工厂单台工业母机满足节能要求，但整条产线因为协同不合理，存在大量的待机能耗、空转能耗，整体能效仍然偏低；现在通过一体化协同优化，可以让整个柔性制造单元的所有装备节拍匹配，减少无效能耗，整体能效可以再提升10%左右。
6. 支持绿色再制造与循环经济
新设计生产的工业母机必须考虑后期的再制造需求，通过模块化设计方便核心部件的修复、更换和智能化改造，让废旧机床可以通过翻新改造恢复高性能状态，而不是直接报废回炉，大幅降低制造业的设备采购成本和资源消耗[1]。目前国内机床保有量超过1000万台，其中大量老旧机床存在精度不够、能耗偏高的问题，如果全部淘汰会造成巨大的资源浪费，而通过绿色再制造，可以让老旧机床满足新的生产要求，成本仅为新机床的30%-50%，节能效果可以达到20%以上，对中小制造企业来说性价比非常高。

智能化技术是实现工业母机绿色制造的核心路径，没有新一代人工智能、传感器、数字孪生等技术的赋能，绿色制造的各项要求都无法落地[1]。
具体来看，目前已经落地的核心技术路径主要分为四个方向：
多模态融合感知技术：在工业母机的关键部位部署各类智能传感器，可以实时监测设备能耗、切削液状态、刀具磨损、主轴负载等各类参数，为能效优化和碳核算提供准确的基础数据，这是所有绿色功能的基础。如果没有准确的实时数据，AI优化和碳足迹追踪都无从谈起[1]。AI实时补偿与动态优化：通过训练好的工业AI算法，根据多模态传感器采集的实时数据，自动调整加工参数、进给速度、主轴转速，在保证加工精度和质量的前提下，尽可能减少能源和耗材的浪费，实现能效的动态最优。和传统固定参数加工相比，AI动态优化可以在不影响生产效率的前提下降低能耗，实现了绿色和效益的平衡。\li>
数字孪生技术：在工业母机加工新产品之前，可以先在数字孪生模型中进行工艺预演，找到最优的加工路径和参数，避免实体试切过程中的材料浪费和能源消耗，对于大型复杂零部件加工来说，这一优势尤其明显，可以减少至少30%的试切浪费[1]。预测性维护技术：通过AI模型提前预测设备故障，提前安排维护计划，减少非计划停机带来的能源损耗和材料浪费。非计划停机不仅会影响生产效率，还会造成工件报废、反复开机能耗增加等问题，预测性维护可以将非计划停机时间降低50%以上，间接实现了显著的节能降碳效果。值得注意的是，此次发布的《工业母机智能化变革十大趋势展望（2026）》还提到，除了绿色制造相关技术，新一代人工智能技术还在从底层重塑工业母机的技术逻辑：大语言模型、工业智能体等技术已经开始嵌入工业母机，未来的智能工业母机将从“被动执行指令的工具”转变为“自主完成制造任务的物理智能体”，绿色制造也将从“人为设定规则”转变为“工业母机自主优化能效”，技术迭代的空间非常大[1]。
另一个值得关注的技术趋势是数控系统的开放化转型：目前国内外主流数控厂商都在推动数控系统从封闭专用向“云边端”开放平台化架构转型，开放的架构可以让第三方厂商更方便地加载AI能效优化、碳足迹追踪等绿色智能功能，降低了绿色功能的开发和适配成本，也会加速绿色制造技术在存量工业母机上的推广应用[1]。
绿色制造要求会给工业母机行业带来哪些影响？
2026年绿色制造刚性要求的落地，正在从根本上重塑我国工业母机行业的竞争格局，推动行业加速向高端化、智能化、绿色化方向转型[4]。
首先，绿色制造已经成为新的行业准入门槛，大量中小工业母机厂商如果无法在短期内跟上绿色转型的要求，将会逐步被市场淘汰。过去很多中小厂商依靠低成本、低价格抢占市场，产品只满足基本的加工要求，不具备绿色功能，现在下游用户采购都要求绿色指标，这些没有绿色技术能力的厂商将会逐步退出市场，行业集中度会进一步提升。
其次，绿色转型催生了新的产业机会，除了新机床的绿色升级，存量机床的绿色再制造也成为一个快速崛起的新赛道。我国目前有超过1000万台的存量机床，其中超过40%的机床使用年限超过10年，这些机床普遍存在能耗高、精度差的问题，都需要进行绿色智能化改造，市场规模超过千亿元，给再制造厂商、智能化改造服务商带来了巨大的市场机会。
第三，绿色制造推动工业母机行业的价值模式从卖产品向卖服务转型。过去工业母机厂商主要靠卖整机赚钱，现在随着碳足迹追踪、能效优化等服务的普及，越来越多的厂商开始推出“能效按效果分成”等服务模式，比如帮助下游企业降低能耗，从中分成收益，这改变了行业的价值创造逻辑，也给厂商带来了持续的收入来源。
从更宏观的层面来看，工业母机的绿色转型，也为我国整个制造业实现双碳目标提供了核心装备支撑。制造业是我国能源消耗和碳排放的主要领域，而工业母机是制造业的源头装备，工业母机的能效每降低10%，可以带动下游制造业整体能耗降低3%-5%，带动效应非常明显，对我国完成双碳目标具有重要的战略意义[4]。
当然，行业转型也面临一些现实的挑战：一是绿色设计和智能化功能会推高工业母机的生产成本，导致新机床售价上涨，部分中小制造企业对采购新的绿色工业母机存在一定的资金压力；二是目前碳足迹核算的行业标准还在逐步完善过程中，不同厂商的碳足迹数据还存在口径不统一的问题，需要进一步规范；三是绿色技术的人才储备不足，既懂工业母机又懂绿色设计和AI技术的复合型人才比较短缺，需要时间培养。
整体来看，这些挑战都是发展中的问题，随着政策的落地、行业标准的完善和技术的进步，都会逐步得到解决。从长期趋势来看，高端化、智能化、绿色化是我国工业母机行业确定的发展方向，绿色制造要求的落地，会加速这一进程，推动我国工业母机产业实现从大到强的跨越，也会为我国制造业高质量发展提供更坚实的支撑[4]。

title: 湘潭首张湘林碳票挂牌上市 林业碳汇接入省级交易平台
summary: 湘潭湘乡市2026年度湘林碳票项目挂牌上市，初始签发碳减排量7.34万吨CO2e，探索“以碳代偿”生态修复新模式，盘活300余万亩林地资源。
content:
7月6日，湘乡市湘林碳票在湖南联合产权交易所挂牌上市，标志着湘潭市林业碳汇成功接入省级交易平台，当地林业资源向资产、资金转化迈出关键一步。
湘林碳票是指湖南省内权属清晰的林地、林木所产生的碳汇量（一定时期内森林碳库碳储量的变化量），经林业部门计量、审核、登记而制发的温室气体减排量凭证，被赋予交易、融资、抵消碳排放等权能。
此次上市的湘乡市2026年度湘林碳票项目，已于5月26日顺利签发。项目覆盖翻江镇、东郊乡等地，林地总面积917.51公顷，初始签发碳减排量73430.6吨二氧化碳当量，计入期为2026年至2030年，预计可实现碳汇收入近600万元。
此次挂牌迎来湘潭碳票首笔实质性业务。上市当日，湘潭县与湘乡市启动湘林碳票购买协商，将以碳票交易替代生态损害补偿，探索“以碳代偿”生态修复新模式，有效衔接生态价值转化与生态损害法律责任，进一步拓宽了碳票多元化应用场景。
湘乡市今年1月获省林业局批复，成为全省首批7个湘林碳票推广试点市之一。依托湘乡先行先试经验，湘潭市统筹推进湘潭县、韶山市、雨湖区、岳塘区碳票开发工作，目前各区域正有序开展资源调查、碳汇潜力核算、项目框架搭建等前期工作。此次碳票市场化落地，将盘活湘潭市300余万亩林地资源，构建“碳汇开发—交易变现—反哺林农”的绿色良性循环，为乡村振兴持续注入生态动能。
（文/颜石敦 钟佳燊 刘运良 李炜亿）

title: 中经评论：碳达峰行动释放更多“绿色红利”
summary: 评论指出“十五五”碳达峰行动方案释放清晰信号：推进碳达峰是转换发展赛道，在绿色变革中释放经济与民生红利，绿色低碳产业市场规模有望破20万亿元。
content:
中经评论：碳达峰行动释放更多“绿色红利”中国经济网
2026-07-16 07:20发布于 北京中国经济网官方账号
戈壁滩上一排排风机拔地而起，屋顶光伏逐步走进千家万户，通勤路上越来越多新能源汽车穿梭街巷……“双碳”目标提出以来，低碳转型持续渗透生产生活。国务院近日印发的《“十五五”碳达峰行动方案》（以下简称《方案》）强调，发挥碳达峰碳中和战略牵引作用，加快形成绿色生产生活方式，培育更多绿色经济增长点。《方案》传递出一个清晰信号：推进碳达峰绝非放慢发展脚步，而是转换发展赛道，在绿色变革中释放经济与民生红利。
统筹能源安全与绿色转型，是《方案》锚定的核心任务，也是“双碳”战略发挥牵引作用的核心战场。我国能源转型任务繁重，煤炭、石油消费稳步达峰是阶段性硬性目标，新增用能需求离不开清洁能源支撑。按照《方案》部署，到“十五五”时期末，我国非化石能源消费比重提升至25%。庞大转型目标背后，是一条万亿级产业赛道，光伏、风电、储能、特高压智能电网上下游产业链协同发力，制造、研发、运维、服务完整业态不断扩容。依托完整工业体系优势，我国清洁能源装备产业将持续领跑全球，绿色能源不再只是保障国内用能需求的基础支撑，更成为参与全球竞争的核心优势产业。
传统重工业同样迎来转型升级契机。《方案》引导钢铁、化工、建材等行业告别粗放规模扩张，向低碳化、高端化、精细化方向转型。企业通过高炉低碳改造、原料循环利用、余热回收等技术革新，在压缩碳排放的同时，提升产品附加值，淘汰低效落后产能，留存优质先进产能，实现“减重提质”。
数字技术 与绿色低碳深度融合，进一步放大转型效能。 工业互联网 、能耗监测大数据、碳足迹溯源系统走进生产车间，数字化赋能精准节能，催生节能诊断、碳管理咨询、低碳装备改造等新业态，持续拓宽绿色经济增长空间。据测算，“十五五”时期末国内绿色低碳产业整体市场规模有望突破20万亿元，绿色赛道正成为经济增长的核心增量。
碳达峰行动带来的“绿色红利”，每个人都能直观感知。出行场景的变革正在加速落地，《方案》明确：到2030年，新能源汽车保有量占比力争达到30%，新能源营运交通工具保有量占比达到25%。新能源汽车普及不只是环保选择，更是实实在在的民生实惠，更低的充电成本、简化的维保流程，持续降低大众出行开销，配套充电桩、换电站城乡全覆盖，彻底打消新能源汽车出行的里程焦虑。
居住场景的低碳升级，重塑居家生活体验。《方案》推进建筑光伏一体化、绿色低碳冷暖供应、全域高效照明改造，城镇新建建筑全面执行绿色建筑标准。未来居民住宅既能依托屋顶光伏自发自用、余电上网，又能依靠高效温控设备减少能源消耗，在不降低居住舒适度的前提下，实现居家用能绿色化。
绿色转型还将催生全新职业赛道，一批“绿领”新职业走入大众视野。风光电站运维技师、碳核算分析师、低碳建筑设计师、工业节能改造工程师、林业碳汇管理员等岗位需求持续扩张。过去冷门的环境、能源相关专业，成为就业热门选择。传统行业从业者也迎来转型机遇，工厂技工转型节能设备运维，地产设计师深耕零碳建筑研发，低碳产业扩容不断拓宽就业渠道，创造多元职业选择。

title: 力促让群众吃得放心、住得安心——解读《土壤、地下水和农业农村生态环境保护“十五五”规划》
source: 中国政府网 · 国务院政策文件库
summary: 新华社北京7月17日电 题：力促让群众吃得放心、住得安心——解读《土壤、地下水和农业农村生态环境保护“十五五”规划》 新华社记者 高敬 生态环境部等六部门联合印发《土壤、地下水和农业农村生态环境保护“...
content:
力促让群众吃得放心、住得安心——解读《土壤、地下水和农业农村生态环境保护“十五五”规划》
2026-07-18 09:14
字号：默认
新华社北京7月17日电 题：力促让群众吃得放心、住得安心——解读《土壤、地下水和农业农村生态环境保护“十五五”规划》
新华社记者 高敬
生态环境部等六部门联合印发《土壤、地下水和农业农村生态环境保护“十五五”规划》。规划按照控新增、减存量、防风险、保安全、促健康的总体思路，明确目标指标和工作部署，力促让群众吃得放心、住得安心。生态环境部土壤生态环境司负责人就规划有关问题进行了解读。
针对性措施管控建设用地土壤污染风险
建设用地土壤安全状况备受公众关注。这位负责人介绍，“十四五”时期，各地加强建设用地准入管理，保障近5万个用途变更为居住、公共管理与公共服务用地的重点建设用地安全利用。“十五五”期间，建设用地土壤污染防治按照“严防新增、控减存量、安全利用”的思路，采取系列针对性保障措施，保障人民群众“住得安心”。
严防企业新增土壤污染。以化工等行业为重点，从推动产业转型升级、强化多要素协同防治、加强土壤污染重点监管单位管理等方面，突出源头防控，将土壤污染遏制在责任主体明晰且具备治理能力和资金保障的企业存续阶段。
严控腾退地块污染风险。强化建设用地土壤污染风险管控和修复名录制度，健全全过程质量管理，针对沿江1公里等重点区域和农药原药制造等重点行业地块，开展专项治理，分类管控污染。
保障再开发地块安全利用。推动建设用地土壤环境管理要求纳入供地管理。强化“存量优先”用地理念，通过分期分片治理、分层开发管控等方式，推动地块管控修复与盘活利用有序衔接。
此外，要健全建设用地土壤污染防治法规标准体系，推动完善治用协同机制，强化执法监管等。
加强农用地土壤重金属污染溯源与整治
这位负责人介绍，“十五五”是农用地土壤重金属污染防治关键期。生态环境部将指导各地降低土壤重金属累积性风险，推动农用地土壤环境质量稳中向好，保障老百姓“吃得放心”。
他表示，要以县为基本单位，按年度分解落实农用地土壤重金属污染溯源和整治任务，强化调度推进、项目支持、监督考核，扎实完成目标。要精准溯源，聚焦人为污染源，充分利用信息技术，开展实地调查和监测分析，追溯现有和历史遗留污染源，建立并动态更新源清单。
在系统整治方面，严格在产企业重金属排放监管，推进历史遗留污染源整治。对大气输入型污染，划定重点区域，执行颗粒物、重金属污染物特别排放限值，推动工艺设备和废气处理设施升级改造；对水输入型污染，在土壤污染防治资金支持下，地方加大投入力度，重点整治历史遗留废渣及受污染水体底泥，优先采用低扰动、成熟可靠、经济实用的整治技术。
此外要开展土壤重金属含量、大气重金属沉降、农田灌溉水质监测，综合评估整治成效，切断镉等重金属污染物进入农田的链条。
推动地下水环境质量稳中向好
据这位负责人介绍，“十四五”时期，我国地下水污染治理成效逐步显现，全国地下水国控点位Ⅰ—Ⅳ类水比例稳定在75%左右。
“十五五”期间要构建水源与区域、污染源与区域、资源与环境三大协同体系，推动地下水环境质量稳中向好。
——强化水源与区域环境协同保护。筛查全氟化合物、重金属等潜在污染风险，划定地下水污染防治重点区，实现从“保单一水源”到“护区域水资源”的战略延伸。
——开展污染源与区域污染协同防控。开展全国地下水污染调查评价，深化污染源管控，建设污染防治先导区，探索区域治理路径。
——探索地下水资源与环境协同管控。强化地下水回补、泉域保护、矿产资源开发等领域地下水环境保护，统筹地下水资源保护与污染防治。
对农业面源污染突出区域推动系统治理
农业面源污染量大面广，与群众生产生活关联密切。
这位负责人表示，要聚焦问题突出区域推动系统治理。各地统筹稳产保供、农民增收和生态环境保护，持续提升污染防治成效。加强水源地、溶洞周边及河道沿岸畜禽粪污直排乱堆问题巡查监管，强化喀斯特地区畜禽养殖经营主体污染监管。
同时，要着力提升问题发现能力，充分利用遥感监测、人工智能筛选、投诉举报分析等非现场手段，及时发现和推动解决一批严重影响群众生活的畜禽养殖污染问题。
在污染源头防治方面，将推动地方依法确定散养密集区，鼓励因地制宜以村屯或乡镇为单位进行粪污集中堆沤和还田利用。此外，要加强畜禽养殖场（户）污染防治宣传指导，引导落实主体责任。

title: Transversalité pour la circularité et la sobriété à Grenoble
source: HAL (Le Centre pour la Communication Scientifique Directe)
summary: SSH CENTRE (Social Sciences and Humanities for Climate, Energy aNd Transport Research Excellence) is a Horizon Europe project, engaging directly with stakeholders across research, policy, and business (including citizens) to strengthen soci
content: SSH CENTRE (Social Sciences and Humanities for Climate, Energy aNd Transport Research Excellence) is a Horizon Europe project, engaging directly with stakeholders across research, policy, and business (including citizens) to strengthen social innovation, SSH-STEM collaboration, transdisciplinary policy advice, inclusive engagement, and SSH communities across Europe, accelerating the EU’s transition to carbon neutrality. SSH CENTRE is based in a range of activities related to Open Science, inclusivity and diversity – especially with regards Southern and Eastern Europe and different career stages – including: development of novel SSH-STEM collaborations to facilitate the delivery of the EU Green Deal; SSH knowledge brokerage to support regions in transition; and the effective design of strategies for citizen engagement in EU R&I activities. Outputs include action-led agendas and building stakeholder synergies through regular Policy Insight events.This is captured in a high-profile virtual SSH CENTRE generating and sharing best practice for SSH policy advice, overcoming fragmentation to accelerate the EU’s journey to a sustainable future. The documents uploaded here are outputs from the SSH CENTRE's Knowledge Brokerage programme. Through the KB programme, six teams of PhD and Early Career Researchers were partnered with a European municipality to undertake a Knowledge Brokerage Initiative. The Knowledge Brokerage Initiatives undertaken related to key challenges of the EU Green Deal, namely: local climate strategies; resource efficiency/sufficiency and circular economy; Energy Communities; fossil-free heating and cooling; Mobility Communities; and, digital mobility platforms. The report uploaded here is from the Knowledge Brokerage Initiative undertaken in Grenoble, France, which focused on circularity and sufficiency. The report provides a summary of the activities organised by the researcher team, findings from the activities undertaken, and recommendations for Grenoble based upon these insights. Activities completed as part of the Knowledge Brokerage Initiative include a survey with Grenoble municipality employees and a workshop with municipality representatives across Europe. The report is also available in English.

title: Thermocatalytic transcarbonation with diethyl carbonate for valorization of glycerol : recycling siliceous bauxite residue waste components and exploring the potential of sodalite hydroxide reservoir
source: Repository of the Academy's Library (Library of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences)
summary: Bauxite residues contain katoites and desilication products (sodalite and cancrinite), which are excellent candidates for Earth-abundant heterogeneous base catalysts from industrial waste sources. For the first time, they were tested in syn
content: Bauxite residues contain katoites and desilication products (sodalite and cancrinite), which are excellent candidates for Earth-abundant heterogeneous base catalysts from industrial waste sources. For the first time, they were tested in synthetizing the renewable and promising fuel or fuel additive glycerol carbonate for the purpose of recycling glycerol by-products from biodiesel production. Incorporation of silicate was found to enhance the previously established excellent catalytic activity of tricalcium aluminate (Si-free katoite). Performance of sodalites containing four different cage anion-designed (OH, CO3, SO4, Cl) and carbonated cancrinite was determined to a much greater extent by their Brönsted OH content than by the basicity of the caged anions. Direct catalytic use of bauxite residue resulted in a glycerol carbonate yield of over 80%, but it was quickly deactivated due to the limited reusability of many of its most active components (i.e., Si-free and Si-containing katoites, chloride sodalites). However, hydroxysodalites showed excellent reusability, with a glycerol carbonate yield of around 80% even after 5 reuses. The activity of katoites and sodalities overtook that of many complex systems containing relatively rare metals, such as Ni, Cu, Zr, and Ce. Their excellent activity has made it possible to use diethyl carbonate solvent/reagent, which is more favourable in terms of sustainability, instead of the more widely applied dimethyl carbonate, even with as short reaction times as 30–60 min.

title: Design and Development of Dry Powder Cyclodextrin Complexes of Zinc Diethyldithiocarbamate for Pulmonary Drug Delivery
summary: Background: Pulmonary drug delivery represents a promising approach for the potential localised treatment of respiratory of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the efficient delivery of poorly water-soluble drugs remains challengin
content: Background: Pulmonary drug delivery represents a promising approach for the potential localised treatment of respiratory of non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC). However, the efficient delivery of poorly water-soluble drugs remains challenging due to limited solubility and inadequate aerodynamic performance. This study aimed to develop and characterise inhalable dry powder formulations of zinc diethyldithiocarbamate (Zn(DDC)2) complexes with hydroxypropyl-β-cyclodextrin (HP-β-CD) and sulfobutylether-β-cyclodextrin (SBE-β-CD) for potential pulmonary administration. Methods: Formulations were prepared by freeze-drying and spray-drying, with leucine incorporated at 0%, 5%, and 10% w/w. Formulations were prepared via freeze-drying and spray-drying with leucine incorporation (0%, 5% and 10% w/w) to evaluate their physicochemical properties, flowability and aerodynamic performance. Results: Spray-dried formulations exhibited significantly lower densities (as low as 1.03 ± 0.71 g/cm3), enhanced flowability, improved aerosolisation and higher fine particle fraction (FPF) values (up to 40.12 ± 0.60%) compared to freeze-dried powders (20.03 ± 2.79%). The incorporation of leucine further reduced powder density down to 0.72 ± 0.34 g/cm3 and increased surface corrugation as shown in SEM images, improving aerosolisation performance, with FPF values up to 76.77 ± 1.18%. Next Generation Impactor (NGI) analysis confirmed that leucine-containing formulations exhibited a greater proportion of particles within the respirable aerodynamic diameter range (1–5 μm), suggesting suitability for deep lung deposition. Conclusions: These results demonstrate that spray-dried Zn(DDC)2–cyclodextrin powders, particularly those modified with 10% leucine, offer excellent potential for pulmonary delivery in NSCLC therapy. Further in vivo studies are warranted to evaluate therapeutic efficacy and safety.

title: Reconfiguring Fashion through Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities, Ethics and Emerging Challenges
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping contemporary fashion by transforming design processes, production systems, and sustainability strategies in the textile and apparel sector. Amid growing concerns over overconsumption, environmental
content: Artificial Intelligence (AI) is reshaping contemporary fashion by transforming design processes, production systems, and sustainability strategies in the textile and apparel sector. Amid growing concerns over overconsumption, environmental degradation, carbon emissions, and social inequities, AI has emerged as both a technological enabler and a subject of ethical scrutiny. This study examines the influence of AI on creative practice, circular design implementation, and responsible innovation in fashion. Drawing on a qualitative synthesis of systematic literature, design theory, and industry case analyses, this study proposes a framework that situates AI within sustainable fashion discourse. Findings indicate that generative design tools, virtual prototyping, digital twins, and predictive analytics support waste reduction, virtual sampling, demand-responsive production, and informed material selection. AI-enabled resale systems, automated textile sorting, and blockchain-based traceability strengthen circular economy initiatives by extending product lifecycles and improving transparency. However, algorithmic decision-making challenges authorship, craftsmanship, dataset neutrality, and labor structures. Concerns over bias, intellectual property ambiguity, digital energy consumption, and workforce displacement complicate sustainability narratives. The study argues that sustainable transformation requires a human-centered governance approach in which AI augments rather than replaces creative agency and is supported by ethical regulation and critical design education. By integrating sustainability theory, computational creativity, and AI ethics, this research contributes a holistic framework for responsible AI adoption in fashion systems.

title: Promoting Electroreduction CO <sub>2</sub> to Multi‐Carbon Products by Tailoring the <sup>*</sup> H Availability With Optimized Interfacial H <sub>2</sub> O Configuration
summary: ABSTRACT The electroreduction of CO 2 to multi‐carbon products provides a promising path for approaching carbon neutrality. H 2 O is generally considered a hydrogen source in CO 2 RR, tailoring the interfacial H 2 O configuration is critica
content: ABSTRACT The electroreduction of CO 2 to multi‐carbon products provides a promising path for approaching carbon neutrality. H 2 O is generally considered a hydrogen source in CO 2 RR, tailoring the interfacial H 2 O configuration is critical yet often overlooked strategy for modulating CO 2 RR performance. In this work, we demonstrated that regulating the interfacial water configuration through ionomer confinement is an effective strategy for enhancing multi‐carbon (C 2+ ) product selectivity in CO 2 RR. The optimized catalyst 15.79% A5‐Cu achieves 82% Faradaic efficiency (FE) for C 2+ products at 200 mA cm −2 in 0.1 M KHCO 3 and operates stably for over 100 h without salt precipitation in MEA system. In situ ATR‐SEIRAS and Raman spectroscopy revealed that the confined environment tunes the proportion between K + ‐H 2 O and 4‐HB‐H 2 O configuration of interfacial H 2 O. This enhanced *H generation and transfer ability can improve the *H utilization efficiency. Moreover, a moderate *H availability constructed by the balanced proportion of K + ‐H 2 O and 4‐HB‐H 2 O configurations lowers the energy barrier for *CO hydrogenation and subsequently C─C coupling step at a higher *CO coverage, which was confirmed by DFT calculations. This work highlights the critical role of interfacial H 2 O configuration in steering C 2+ product selectivity for that in addition to *H generation, the hydrogen bonding network can accurately guide *H toward *CO intermediate, thereby avoiding excessive accumulation of *H species.

title: Greenhouse gas emissions from rice crop production in Jiangxi Province (China) based on life cycle assessment and household panel data
summary: Accurately understanding the current status and driving factors of agricultural greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from rice crop production in China is crucial for achieving the national “dual carbon” goals. Based on a farm household panel dat
content: Accurately understanding the current status and driving factors of agricultural greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions from rice crop production in China is crucial for achieving the national “dual carbon” goals. Based on a farm household panel dataset collected in Jiangxi Province from 2018 to 2023, the study employs Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) approach to calculate GHG emissions from rice crop production at the household level and further analyzes driving factors of GHG emissions using a two-way fixed effects model. CH 4 emissions from rice planting, CO 2 emissions from electricity used for irrigation, and N 2 O emissions from nitrogen fertilizer application are the main sources of rice crop production GHG emissions. GHG emission intensity from rice crop production at the household level first declined and then increased from 2018 to 2023. The GHG emission intensity gap among farmers has widened during this period. Notably, GHG emission intensity of early rice crop production is significantly lower than that of late rice crop production. An increase in rice TFP was found to be the key factor in reducing GHG emissions. It demonstrated a “U-shaped” relationship between planting size and GHG emission intensity. Additionally, implementing green agricultural subsidy schemes was found to reduce GHG emission intensity significantly. On the contrary, using organic soil amendments tended to increase GHG emission intensity. The study suggests encouraging farmers to improve water, energy, and fertilizer management in rice crop production and optimize production input factors.

title: Beyond a single path: A meta-theoretical review of how spatial, political, and institutional dynamics shape China's net-zero transition
summary: How can we comprehend China's net-zero transition approach when distinct theoretical frameworks offer differing explanations? Drawn from extensive original field research and 52 semi-structured interviews with experts on China, we apply a m
content: How can we comprehend China's net-zero transition approach when distinct theoretical frameworks offer differing explanations? Drawn from extensive original field research and 52 semi-structured interviews with experts on China, we apply a meta-theoretical approach that first describes three complementary frameworks (Geographies of Energy Transition, Variegated Capitalism, and Fragmented Authoritarianism) to interpret China's net-zero transition under the dual “30–60” targets of peaking emissions by 2030 and reaching carbon neutrality by 2060. The Geographies of Energy Transition approach reveals the spatial differentiation, path dependence, and regional unevenness embedded in China's net-zero transition. Variegated Capitalism highlights a state-led logic of “managed competition”, in which state-owned enterprises, party authority, and relational ( guanxi ) networks enable multi-level policy coordination and technological mobilization. Meanwhile, Fragmented Authoritarianism underscores the coexistence of centralization and decentralization within China's administrative state, illustrating the misalignments, negotiations, and experimental practices that characterize policy implementation. After describing each of these theories, we discuss and demonstrate how framework pluralism reveals insights unavailable to single-perspective analysis; empirically, we provide evidence across multiple domains and sectors; methodologically, we show that net-zero transitions are multi-dimensional phenomena that defy any singular framework attempting to explain China's transitions. Although we do not offer a synthesis of these theories, bringing together different perspectives demonstrates that net-zero transitions are neither teleological, in the sense of operating according to a fixed internal logic and timetable, nor unitary processes. Instead, they are marked by political ruptures, multi-scalar interactions and contestations, unanticipated technological dynamics, and very distinct ideological underpinnings.

title: From Biomass to Functional Gels: Multiscale Topology Reconstruction and High‐Performance Applications
summary: ABSTRACT With over 400 million tons of plastic waste generated annually, developing advanced soft matter from renewable biomass is critical for carbon neutrality. Bio‐based gels offer exceptional biocompatibility and degradability, emerging
content: ABSTRACT With over 400 million tons of plastic waste generated annually, developing advanced soft matter from renewable biomass is critical for carbon neutrality. Bio‐based gels offer exceptional biocompatibility and degradability, emerging as sustainable alternatives to petroleum‐based polymers. However, native biopolymers suffer from weak mechanical properties, poor environmental adaptability, and limited functionality, restricting their practical applications. To overcome these bottlenecks, recent research focuses on multiscale network topology reconstruction and synergistic enhancement of dynamic interactions. This review constructs a comprehensive framework from “biomass raw materials” to “functionalized design” and “high‐value applications.” We elucidate microscopic mechanisms driving toughening, self‐healing, and extreme environmental tolerance, including dual‐network entanglement, nanocomposites, and medium engineering. Furthermore, we discuss transformative applications of functionalized bio‐based gels in biomedical engineering, flexible electronics, environmental remediation, smart packaging, and green energy storage.

title: High-Accuracy Determination of Coal Quality Parameters Using Dual-Pulse Laser-Induced Breakdown Spectroscopy (DP-LIBS) Combined with Machine Learning Algorithms
summary: Rapid and accurate determination of quality parameters (carbon content, ash, volatile matter, and calorific value) is essential for the clean and efficient utilization of coal. In this work, an innovative strategy combining dual-pulse laser
content: Rapid and accurate determination of quality parameters (carbon content, ash, volatile matter, and calorific value) is essential for the clean and efficient utilization of coal. In this work, an innovative strategy combining dual-pulse laser-induced breakdown spectroscopy (DP-LIBS) with machine learning algorithms is proposed. Through systematic optimization of critical parameters, including laser wavelengths (1064 + 532 nm), pulse energy distribution (50 + 20 mJ), pulse interval (0.5 μs), and sampling distance (9.9 cm), spectral signal intensity and signal-to-noise ratio are significantly enhanced. Furthermore, by integrating spectral preprocessing (wavelet denoising, baseline correction, and Z-score normalization) with partial least squares regression, random forest, support vector machine regression (SVMR), and k-nearest neighbor, a high-precision coal quality prediction framework is presented. The experimental results demonstrate that under DP-LIBS conditions, the SVMR algorithm significantly reduces the prediction error for carbon content with a mean relative error (MRE) of 3.05% and a root mean square error of prediction of 2.44%, and yields optimal performance for calorific value prediction with an MRE of 3.74%. This work provides a high-throughput, low-error solution for online coal quality detection, advancing the practical application of LIBS technology in energy quality monitoring and carbon neutrality pathways.

title: Campus as Carbon Sink
summary: Soils are a major carbon sink, and as atmospheric carbon emissions continue to increase around the world, attention is being turned to soils as a possible way to offset these emissions. For institutions like colleges and universities that m
content: Soils are a major carbon sink, and as atmospheric carbon emissions continue to increase around the world, attention is being turned to soils as a possible way to offset these emissions. For institutions like colleges and universities that manage significant acreage and are increasingly seeking avenues toward carbon neutrality, quantifying and enhancing the amount of carbon held in campus soil may be a valuable addition to existing sustainability efforts. This study investigates how land cover and soil compaction affect soil carbon sequestration on a college campus in the Southeastern U.S. Areas of different land covers in one campus neighborhood were mapped using GIS software to determine predominant landscaping conditions. Grassy lawns covered 67.4% of the study area, perennial beds covered 22.9%, and annual beds covered 2.1%, making up the vast majority of permeable surface area. Compaction measurements and soil samples were taken from randomly selected points within each of these three land cover types. Soil samples were analyzed using Loss-on-Ignition (LOI) techniques to determine the percentage of soil organic carbon (SOC) by mass. Findings showed that compaction is strongly correlated with land cover, prohibiting the distinction between the impact of land cover vs. compaction on SOC content. Perennial beds were moderately compacted and contain more SOC than grassy lawns (average 8.02% vs. 6.37%) which were highly compacted. Annual beds were minimally compacted and showed the highest average SOC values of 23.97%, likely due to large inputs of compost rather than long-term biological soil carbon sequestration. The results of this study suggest that conversion of grassy lawns into perennial plant beds would increase SOC sequestration potential on campus, thereby contributing to university carbon neutrality goals by sequestering atmospheric carbon in the ground.

title: Research on the Relationship Among Corporate ESG Performance, Digital Transformation and Green Innovation
summary: Driven by China’s carbon peak and carbon neutrality targets as well as sustainable development strategies, green innovation has attracted widespread attention. As a comprehensive indicator, ESG can establish correlations with green innovati
content: Driven by China’s carbon peak and carbon neutrality targets as well as sustainable development strategies, green innovation has attracted widespread attention. As a comprehensive indicator, ESG can establish correlations with green innovation through resource allocation and other channels. Using data from Chinese A-share listed companies over 2010–2024, this paper empirically examines the impact and mechanism of ESG ratings on corporate green innovation. The results indicate that the improvement of ESG rating significantly promotes corporate green innovation. The impact intensifies among large firms, light-polluting industries, and technologically mature sectors. Mechanism tests indicate that ESG can enhance green innovation output by boosting corporate digital transformation and alleviating financing constraints. The findings provide empirical evidence and practical enlightenment for regulators to improve the ESG disclosure system and for enterprises to implement green development strategies.

title: Pengembangan Model Produksi Eco-Enzyme Berbasis Limbah Dapur Hotel sebagai Strategi Operasional Berkelanjutan di Ts Suites Seminyak Bali
source: Jurnal Ekonomi Manajemen Pariwisata dan Perhotelan
summary: This study aims to develop a hotel kitchen waste-based Eco-enzyme production model as a sustainable operational strategy at TS Suites Seminyak Bali. The study used a descriptive qualitative approach with an applied case study design. Data w
content: This study aims to develop a hotel kitchen waste-based Eco-enzyme production model as a sustainable operational strategy at TS Suites Seminyak Bali. The study used a descriptive qualitative approach with an applied case study design. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, field observation, documentation, and review of operational documents. Informants were selected purposively from management, kitchen, stewarding, food and beverage, housekeeping public area, engineering, purchasing or cost control, human resources, and related operational units. The data were analyzed thematically through data reduction, data display, conclusion drawing, and verification. Data credibility was strengthened through source, technique, and document triangulation. The findings show that the hotel already has a basic flow for collecting and sorting kitchen waste, but it is not yet supported by a specific SOP, consistent organic waste volume records, and cross-department monitoring. The developed model consists of seven main components: sorting suitable organic materials, applying the formula of 3 kg fruit and vegetable waste : 1 liter molasses : 10 liters water, assigning a person in charge, providing a safe fermentation area, using a production logbook, testing limited operational use, and conducting periodic evaluation. The study concludes that Eco-enzyme can strengthen green operation, circular economy principles, and the palemahan value of Tri Hita Karana when applied through clear SOPs, training, supervision, and controlled areas of use.

title: Construction Model, Strategies, and Effectiveness of Carbon Neutrality Micro-Majors in Double First-Class Universities
source: Journal of Education and Educational Research
summary: Against the backdrop of the growing demand for "dual carbon" talents and the accelerated digital and intelligent transformation, the traditional higher education training system struggles to promptly meet the practical needs of the job mark
content: Against the backdrop of the growing demand for "dual carbon" talents and the accelerated digital and intelligent transformation, the traditional higher education training system struggles to promptly meet the practical needs of the job market for interdisciplinary and compound talents. As a crucial exploration in the reform of higher education teaching, the micro-major talent training model has emerged and gradually become an important institutional innovation to enhance the adaptability of talent supply and training flexibility. The lag in the supply of emerging interdisciplinary talents, the imbalance of resources between eastern and western regions, and the lack of international practice have become universal practical dilemmas in the development of higher education. Taking Tongji University's "Climate Change and Carbon Neutrality" micro-major as a research case, this paper conducts a systematic analysis focusing on talent training objectives, curriculum system structure, and implementation mechanisms, aiming to summarize its construction logic and operational characteristics. The research finds that Tongji University's micro-major has established an organizational model of "joint training by three universities", implemented industry-education integration with enterprises in Xinjiang and international enterprises, innovatively set up the form of "synchronous classrooms", and promoted industry-education integration through multiple subjects such as enterprises in Xinjiang and international enterprises, forming a collaborative education mechanism. Meanwhile, by innovatively adopting teaching formats such as "synchronous classrooms", it enhances cross-regional curriculum supply capacity and learning experience, thereby providing high-quality talent support for the "dual carbon" field.

title: Quantum-Chemical Study for Understanding the Low Incorporation of 2-Methylen-1,3-Dioxepane (MDO) in Radical Ring-Opening Copolymerization with Vinyl Monomers
summary: High Resolution Image Download MS PowerPoint Slide Radical ring-opening polymerization (rROP) of cyclic ketene acetals (CKAs), particularly 2-methylene-1,3-dioxepane (MDO), offers a robust pathway to introduce degradable ester linkages into
content: High Resolution Image Download MS PowerPoint Slide Radical ring-opening polymerization (rROP) of cyclic ketene acetals (CKAs), particularly 2-methylene-1,3-dioxepane (MDO), offers a robust pathway to introduce degradable ester linkages into nondegradable vinyl backbones. However, the rational design of these materials is currently hindered by highly comonomer-dependent open-to-closed (ester vs acetal) incorporation ratios. In this study, a rigorous density functional theory (DFT) framework integrating systematic conformational sampling and implicit solvation is employed to establish a unified structure–reactivity map for MDO copolymerization across a diverse set of vinyl monomers. The computational results reveal that while MDO homopolymerization is thermodynamically driven toward quantitative ring opening due to the irreversibility of the open-chain radical, copolymerization is governed by a fine-tuned competition between the kinetic accessibility of vinyl addition and the stability of the resulting cyclic adduct. The closed-propagation barrier is primarily dictated by a SOMO–LUMO interaction, where the electronic nature and α-substitution of the comonomer modulate orbital overlap and energy. Three distinct reactivity regimes are identified: (1) high open incorporation (e.g., MDO, crotonates), where high vinyl barriers and adduct reversibility favor β-scission; (2) intermediate competition (e.g., vinyl acetate); and (3) ring-retention dominance (e.g., acrylates), where rapid vinyl addition and deep thermodynamic stabilization suppress the degradable pathway. This work provides a qualitative molecular basis for the rational selection of comonomers to maximize CKA incorporation in the open form for next-generation sustainable vinyl polymers.

title: Numerical simulation and experimental validation of electron temperature and number density in novel environmentally friendly CF3SO2F/N2 insulating gas mixtures
source: Journal of Physics D Applied Physics
summary: Abstract CF3SO2F is a new type of eco-friendly electrical insulating gas that is expected to replace SF6. Measuring the electron density and electron temperature of the plasma in this gas mixture is of great significance for studying its in
content: Abstract CF3SO2F is a new type of eco-friendly electrical insulating gas that is expected to replace SF6. Measuring the electron density and electron temperature of the plasma in this gas mixture is of great significance for studying its insulating properties and arc-extinguishing capability. In this paper, numerical simulations of arc plasma were first carried out using the minimum Gibbs free energy method to obtain the theoretical results of the plasma particle composition of the CF3SO2F/N2 mixture. Then, the Laser Thomson Scattering method was employed to measure the electron temperature and density of the gas mixture under different mixing ratios, and the re-sults were compared and verified with the arc simulation results. The electron number density exhibits a pronounced increasing trend with temperature. In addition, a higher CF3SO2F ratio leads to an increase in electron number density within the temperature range of 8000–12000 K, thereby enhancing the electrical conductivity and consequently deteriorating the arc-quenching performance. Under the same temperature condition, the electron density shows an increasing trend with the rise of pressure. Meanwhile, the Thomson experimental results are in good agreement with the simulation results. The volumetric heat capacity under different mixing rati-os and gas pressures was calculated based on the particle composition. The results show that the thermal interruption capability of the gas mixture is enhanced with increasing CF3SO2F ratio.

title: Navigating Paradoxes for Strategic Business Models: Toward Shared Automated Vehicles in Europe
summary: ABSTRACT How can paradoxical tensions in the integration of shared automated vehicles in Europe be navigated to build sustainable business models? Prior research often separates economic, social, and environmental dimensions, overlooking ho
content: ABSTRACT How can paradoxical tensions in the integration of shared automated vehicles in Europe be navigated to build sustainable business models? Prior research often separates economic, social, and environmental dimensions, overlooking how their interdependencies generate tensions across organizational levels. Using a multi‐method design, this study combines three expert interviews analyzed using natural language processing as an exploratory structuring tool with a review of relevant literature to examine these tensions. Based on these insights, the study develops a paradox‐based SWOT framework to interpret how such tensions shape sustainable business model development. Its central theoretical contribution is orchestrated scaling, a context‐specific dynamic capability for managing scale and legitimacy tensions through sequenced expansion, transparency by design, and equity‐oriented safeguards. The study contributes to emerging theory on sustainable mobility transitions and offers practical guidance for organizations developing shared automated vehicle services by linking scaling decisions to business model development and environmental safeguards.

title: Can a history of crop rotations improve the prediction of soil organic carbon in the Andes? integrating machine learning multi-annual crop classification as a proxy of soil management
summary: Soil organic carbon (SOC) is a crucial component related to various processes that ensure soil health and function. Its modeling is vital for assessing and monitoring soil degradation caused by the potential impact of agricultural activitie
content: Soil organic carbon (SOC) is a crucial component related to various processes that ensure soil health and function. Its modeling is vital for assessing and monitoring soil degradation caused by the potential impact of agricultural activities.This study aimed to model SOC in the Northern highlands of Peru, characterized by a high amount of SOC, which is being affected by crop expansion. Crop rotation (CR) history was linked to ground-truthed soil data via a multi-year crop classification model trained on data from 534 fields across 2022-2024. Each cropland field was represented as a polygon delineating its boundaries and indicating its dominant crop cover. Time series of multispectral Sentinel-2 Level-2A Top of Canopy imagery were used to derive phenological features-such as the timing of maximum canopy cover and the length of the growing period-based on Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) time series. A Random Forest classifier was used as the baseline model. The cropland classification model demonstrated a strong overall performance, with F1 scores ranging from 0.81 to 0.98 across the different classes. The model performed well for lupin and pasture but scored lower for beans and potatoes. Predictions of cropland classes from 2019 to 2022 were created, resulting in frequency layers that represent crop rotations. Four feature configurations were evaluated: (i) including all features as a benchmark, (ii) excluding climatology, (iii) excluding crop rotation history, and (iv) excluding soil properties. Configurations including all features and excluding crop rotation history showed the highest performance (R2 = 0.63), while those excluding climatology or soil properties performed worse (R2≈0.52--0.53). Although soil features were the most important, fallow frequency emerged as the most critical predictor of SOC in crop rotations. When soil data were excluded, fallow frequency, combined with climatic features, explained over half of the SOC variability. The findings emphasize the importance of incorporating remote sensing-derived CR into SOC mapping efforts.

title: Unlocking Green Potential: The External Enablement of Digital Infrastructure Development on Urban Green Competitiveness
summary: In the era of carbon neutrality, urban competition has evolved from single-dimensional economic rivalry to multidimensional competition emphasizing green and sustainable development. However, it remains unclear whether digital infrastructur
content: In the era of carbon neutrality, urban competition has evolved from single-dimensional economic rivalry to multidimensional competition emphasizing green and sustainable development. However, it remains unclear whether digital infrastructure, the physical backbone of the digital economy, can externally enhance urban green competitiveness. Building on the measurement of urban green competitiveness through the super-efficiency SBM model, this study employs the “Broadband China” policy as an exogenous shock and uses a Staggered difference-in-differences (SDID) model to systematically analyze the impact and mechanisms of digital infrastructure on urban green competitiveness. The SDID model is adopted in this study for the following reason: the Broadband China strategy constitutes a phased rollout policy shock. By treating this policy as a quasi-natural experiment, the SDID framework enables more accurate identification of its causal impact on urban green competitiveness. The results show that the construction of digital infrastructure significantly promotes urban green competitiveness. Further analysis reveals that digital infrastructure enhances green competitiveness primarily through green technological innovation, industrial upgrading, and economic agglomeration, with the effect of economic agglomeration being stronger than that of the other two channels. Heterogeneity analysis shows that moderate government intervention amplifies the green effects of digital infrastructure. Moreover, the direct effect of digital infrastructure on green competitiveness is more significant in western cities than in eastern and central cities. This study provides empirical evidence for optimizing digital infrastructure development and achieving a “dual drive” of digitalization and green transformation.

title: Microalgae-Based Bioremediation of Aquatic Pollutants and Integrating Carbon Sequestration With Eco-Toxicological Safety and Wastewater Valorization
summary: The dual challenge of escalating carbon emissions and increasing aquatic pollution demands integrated biotechnological solutions capable of addressing both environmental and resource recovery goals. Microalgae have emerged as promising cand
content: The dual challenge of escalating carbon emissions and increasing aquatic pollution demands integrated biotechnological solutions capable of addressing both environmental and resource recovery goals. Microalgae have emerged as promising candidates for sustainable carbon sequestration and wastewater treatment. This chapter explores the role of microalgae in bioremediating aquatic pollutants, including heavy metals, pesticides, and industrial effluents, while simultaneously contributing to carbon fixation and biomass production. The integration of microalgal cultivation with wastewater valorization is discussed in the context of circular bioeconomy principles, highlighting opportunities for resource recovery in the form of biofertilizers, biofuels, and bioplastics. Furthermore, the chapter assesses the environmental safety and sustainability of using algal biomass derived from polluted waters. This work provides a holistic view of microalgae-driven environmental biotechnology as a key pathway toward water sustainability and carbon neutrality.

title: Evolution, Application, and Prospects of the Theory of Planned Behavior: A Case Study of Consumers' Green Consumption Behavior
source: Frontiers in Humanities and Social Sciences
summary: Against the backdrop of the "dual carbon" goals and green development, the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) has emerged as a core framework for analyzing consumers' green consumption behavior. This paper systematically traces the evolutiona
content: Against the backdrop of the "dual carbon" goals and green development, the Theory of Planned Behavior (TPB) has emerged as a core framework for analyzing consumers' green consumption behavior. This paper systematically traces the evolutionary trajectory of TPB, from its origins and international development to its localization and application in China. Its core constructs—attitude, subjective norm, and perceived behavioral control—influence green consumption behavior through behavioral intention. The theory has been integrated with other models, such as the Norm Activation Model, and has undergone significant localization. Current research faces challenges including theoretical stagnation, methodological limitations, insufficient exploration of the intention-behavior translation mechanism, and a lack of heterogeneity analysis. Future research should focus on strengthening theoretical synthesis with local contexts, promoting dynamic and diversified methodological approaches, and delving deeper into the behavioral translation mechanisms and heterogeneity to provide theoretical support and practical guidance for cultivating green consumption behavior.

title: Alternative passenger car fleet decarbonisation pathways in Europe
summary: Achieving rapid reductions in real-world CO 2 emissions from road transport requires not only ambitious CO 2 standards for new vehicles, but also policy designs that accelerate fleet turnover and promote electric driving under real-world co
content: Achieving rapid reductions in real-world CO 2 emissions from road transport requires not only ambitious CO 2 standards for new vehicles, but also policy designs that accelerate fleet turnover and promote electric driving under real-world conditions. An open question is whether passenger car fleet decarbonisation can be achieved solely through full electrification or also through plug-in hybrid powertrain configurations that operate predominantly in electric mode. While the European Union's (EU) current CO 2 standards focus on type-approval performance of new vehicles, their climate impacts depend critically on fleet turnover rates, fuel mix, as well as user behaviour, particularly during the transition period up to 2040 when the displacement of internal combustion engine vehicles is most critical. This study uses a scenario-based assessment framework to examine alternative decarbonisation pathways for the EU passenger car fleet up to 2050. Two scenarios are compared: a baseline pathway consistent with the current EU CO 2 standards, and an alternative stylised pathway reflecting possible market responses to the European Commission's Automotive Package. Particular attention is given to the role of plug-in range-extended electric vehicles (PREVs), together with conventional plug-in hybrid electric vehicles (PHEVs), as complementary technologies to pure electric vehicles (PEVs) that may support faster fleet renewal under regulatory flexibility supporting technological neutrality. Results indicate that under favourable conditions, the alternative pathway leads to lower cumulative tailpipe CO 2 emissions than the baseline pathway with reductions of about 8% between 2028 and 2040. However, the results show that these benefits are highly sensitive to real-world use. If PREVs are operated with electric driving shares similar to current use of PHEVs, the gains are substantially reduced and can reverse beyond 2040 in the longer term. Differences relative to the current standards pathway remain limited up to 2040 because older internal combustion engine vehicles still dominate fleet emissions during much of the transition. The results also indicate persistent demand for liquid fuels in mixed electrification pathways, highlighting the importance for achieving decarbonisation targets of low-carbon fuel supply for road transport alongside electrification. Overall, these findings suggest that regulatory flexibility allowing technological neutrality over the next decade does not automatically accelerate or delay decarbonisation. Its effectiveness depends largely on the conditions under which it is implemented, especially real-world electric driving, fleet-turnover dynamics and supporting fuel and electricity pathways, with prudent assumptions suggesting that until 2040 decarbonisation would not be slowed.

title: A Qualitative Examination of ESG Institutionalization in Mediterranean Banking Operations
summary: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) criteria have become central to how banks finance economic activity, manage risk and respond to intensifying regulatory and stakeholder expectations. Yet the way in which ESG becomes institutionali
content: Environmental, Social and Governance (ESG) criteria have become central to how banks finance economic activity, manage risk and respond to intensifying regulatory and stakeholder expectations. Yet the way in which ESG becomes institutionalized inside individual banks, and particularly within the under-examined Greek banking sector, remains poorly understood. This study provides a qualitative examination of ESG institutionalization within a major Greek bank, Alpha Bank, addressing three questions: what drives ESG adoption, how ESG is embedded across banking operations, and how ESG practices are institutionalized in day-to-day activity. Adopting an interpretivist philosophy and a single-case design, the study draws on six semi-structured interviews with Alpha Bank executives spanning strategy, risk, controlling and compliance functions. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, which yielded three themes: ESG criteria adoption factors, the institutionalization of ESG in banking operations, and the institutionalization of ESG practices. The findings show that adoption is propelled by a confluence of regulatory pressure, investor expectations, an internalized sense of social responsibility and market competitiveness, while institutionalization proceeds through governance reform, the creation of dedicated ESG risk functions, transparent reporting, workforce engagement and strategic integration. Persistent obstacles such as data complexity, measurement difficulty, regulatory burden and cost coexist with clear opportunities in risk management, investor attraction, reputation and sustainable growth. The study contributes a granular, context-specific account of ESG institutionalization in Greek banking and offers practical recommendations for the bank, the sector and policymakers.

title: Public transportation and environmental sustainability nodes in TOD-based Mahakam River city planning
summary: This study addresses the growing need for sustainable and integrated transportation systems in East Kalimantan, particularly in the context of low-carbon development and the strategic role of the Mahakam River as a key regional transport co
content: This study addresses the growing need for sustainable and integrated transportation systems in East Kalimantan, particularly in the context of low-carbon development and the strategic role of the Mahakam River as a key regional transport corridor. Despite its potential to support Transit Oriented Development (TOD), the river-based transportation system remains underutilized and lacks integrated planning. This research aims to analyze the reciprocal relationships among four main TOD dimensions: Transportation Accessibility and Integration, Socio-Economic Impact, Environmental and Ecological Sustainability, and Satisfaction and Policy Support. Using an explanatory quantitative approach, a survey of 105 respondents was conducted and analyzed using Random Forest Regression (RFR) to model complex variable interactions. The results show that the Integrated Transport Access model achieved the highest performance ( R 2 = 0.868; MAPE = 7.44%), followed by the Socio-Economic Impact model ( R 2 = 0.744). The Ecological Environment variable consistently emerged as the most influential factor in three out of four models, underscoring the critical role of environmental sustainability in transportation effectiveness and policy acceptance. These findings highlight that successful TOD-based riverfront revitalization requires a balance between transportation development and ecological conservation, supporting Indonesia’s Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The study also suggests that future research should incorporate qualitative approaches and secondary data analysis to further enrich policy recommendations.

title: Research Progress on Bio-Based Polyurethane-Modified Asphalt Technology
summary: Driven by the goals of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, as well as the increasing demand for green construction materials, traditional petroleum-based asphalt can no longer fully meet the requirements of long-life and low-carbon road c
content: Driven by the goals of carbon peaking and carbon neutrality, as well as the increasing demand for green construction materials, traditional petroleum-based asphalt can no longer fully meet the requirements of long-life and low-carbon road construction due to its strong resource dependence, susceptibility to aging, and difficulty in balancing high- and low-temperature performance. Bio-based polyurethane-modified asphalt (Bio-PUMA) uses renewable or waste biomass to construct high-performance polyurethane (PU) networks, providing a new way to improve pavement performance, reduce carbon emissions, and support the sustainable development of road materials. This paper reviews the molecular structural characteristics of bio-based precursors, including vegetable oil, rosin, and lignin, and summarizes their effects on PU network formation, asphalt microphase morphology, and pavement performance. Existing studies show that the functionality, molecular backbone, hydroxyl value, and soft-to-hard segment ratio of bio-based polyols govern the crosslinking density, phase continuity, and asphalt compatibility of polyurethane networks, thereby influencing rutting resistance, cracking resistance, aging resistance, interfacial adhesion, and mixture performance. Current challenges include unstable biomass feedstocks, difficulty in balancing low-temperature toughness and high-temperature strength, limited long-term service data, and incomplete life-cycle assessment. Future studies should focus on precursor standardization, precise molecular design, multiscale performance evaluation, and engineering validation to promote the application of Bio-PUMA in long-life, low-carbon, and large-scale road infrastructure.

title: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) exposure profiles for pregnant women living in urban, rural, and remote areas of Suriname, South America suggest higher serum concentrations in remote rainforest communities
source: Journal of Exposure Science & Environmental Epidemiology
summary: Abstract Background Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are a diverse group of organofluorine compounds used in industrial and consumer applications. The primary route of human exposure to PFAS is ingestion of contaminated food and d
content: Abstract Background Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) are a diverse group of organofluorine compounds used in industrial and consumer applications. The primary route of human exposure to PFAS is ingestion of contaminated food and drinking water, representing a significant and sometimes unavoidable exposure for many populations. Ecotoxicological and epidemiological studies have established associations between PFAS exposures and adverse health effects. Fetal and childhood development is a particularly susceptible window of exposure. Objective We characterized PFAS exposures for pregnant women in Suriname who identified as Indigenous or Tribal Peoples, and we examined regional variations in exposure patterns between urban, rural, and remote populations. Methods We measured 24 PFAS analytes in the blood serum of 100 pregnant Tribal and Indigenous women living in Suriname. Samples were collected from December 2016 to July 2019 and were purposively selected for laboratory analysis. We assessed differences in serum concentrations visually and statistically by location and ethnicity. Results Ten unique PFAS were detected in at least one sample. title: A framework for assessing climate costs and economic benefits of major entertainment events
summary: Abstract We develop a framework for assessing, and achieving, sustainable events from a climate change perspective using welfare economics and the principle of shared responsibility. We apply this framework to two case-studies as illustrati
content: Abstract We develop a framework for assessing, and achieving, sustainable events from a climate change perspective using welfare economics and the principle of shared responsibility. We apply this framework to two case-studies as illustrative examples: an ex-ante analysis of the 2026 FIFA World Cup and an ex-post analysis of the 2024 Coldplay European tour. Our estimates suggest that the consumer welfare gains from both events far exceed the associated emissions costs, although the World Cup may not be viable under some higher carbon cost estimates. In the absence of adequate carbon pricing, we propose that the principle of shared responsibility be applied to reduce emissions. For indirect emissions, which are the source of most emissions, in particular spectator travel, producers should take on much greater responsibility, including using ticket rebates and better event location choice. Producer efforts at reducing indirect emissions can be large (almost half in the case of Coldplay).

title: Volume crystallization of β-cristobalite from CaO–Al2O3–SiO2 glasses—Influence of different nucleation strategies
summary: Abstract This study examines whether different strategies for increasing crystal number density in CaO–Al 2 O 3 –SiO 2 glasses influence the crystallization mechanism of cristobalite and the stabilization of β -cristobalite during cooling t
content: Abstract This study examines whether different strategies for increasing crystal number density in CaO–Al 2 O 3 –SiO 2 glasses influence the crystallization mechanism of cristobalite and the stabilization of β -cristobalite during cooling to room temperature. Four bulk glasses were investigated: two compositions in the mullite primary phase field and two compositions containing the classical nucleating agents ZrO 2 or TiO 2 . Phase formation after heat treatment was analyzed by X-ray diffraction and dilatometry, while the resulting microstructures and local chemical distributions were studied by electron microscopy including energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopic analyses. The mullite-containing glasses crystallize predominantly in the volume and, together with mullite, form β -cristobalite, whereas the ZrO 2 - and TiO 2 -containing glasses show surface crystallization under the conditions studied. For all compositions, heat treatment at 1,250 °C leads to the precipitation of β -cristobalite which does not transform into α -phase during cooling, while higher crystallization temperatures promote partial transformation to α -cristobalite. Among the investigated compositions, the ZrO 2 -containing glass shows the smallest increase in the cristobalite-related dilatometric volume jump after high-temperature treatment. The results show that mullite can promote volume crystallization, whereas ZrO 2 and TiO 2 do not act as nucleating agents in these glasses. The thermal stability of β -cristobalite is controlled by both composition and microstructure.

title: Improving the Performance of Heart Diseases Classifiers using TOPSIS-VIKOR-ENTROPY
source: Journal of Intelligent Decision Making and Information Science
summary: Nowadays, heart diseases are gaining international attention because they are regarded as a potentially fatal epidemic disease with difficult infection control around the world. Large number of models are proposed in the past. Among them ma
content: Nowadays, heart diseases are gaining international attention because they are regarded as a potentially fatal epidemic disease with difficult infection control around the world. Large number of models are proposed in the past. Among them machine learning gained more attention in heart disease prediction. Machine learning (ML) is an intelligent technique that can predict events with reasonable accuracy based on prior experience and learning. Meanwhile, a large number of ML models have been proposed to predict disease cases. As a result, the main challenge of this study requires an evaluation and benchmarking of ML models. Furthermore, no single study has addressed the issue of diagnosis model evaluation and benchmarking. This study, on the other hand, proposed an intelligent methodology to assist health organizations in the selection of heart disease diagnosis system. Benchmarking and evaluating diagnostic models for disease is a time-consuming process. There are numerous criteria to evaluate, some of which are in conflict with one another. Our research is organised as a decision matrix (DM) with ten evaluation criteria and twelve diagnostic models. The multi-criteria decision-making (MCDM) method is used to evaluate and benchmark the various chronic disease diagnostic models in terms of the evaluation criteria. TOPSIS-VIKOR is used for benchmarking and ranking, while Entropy is used to calculate the weights of criteria in an integrated MCDM method. The study's findings revealed that the benchmarking and selection issues associated with heart disease diagnosis models can be effectively addressed by combining Entropy and TOPSIS-VIKOR. Six Machine Learning Algorithms such as Naive Bayes, Artificial Neural Network, SVM, kNN, Logistic Regression, and Decision Tree are discussed for comparative analysis. To evaluate each of the methods used in this study, parameters such as accuracy, F1 score, Recall, Precision are used.The ML algorithms achieve accuracy of 0.862 in Naïve Bayes0.83 in K-Nearest Neighbor, 0.872 in Artificial Neural Network, 0.856 in Support Vector Machine, 0.756 in Decision Tree, 0.79 in Logistic Regression. From the results it is shown that the Artificial Neural Network classifier was chosen as the best diagnosis model for heart disease

title: Does the CEO–Chairperson Dialect Connection Affect Corporate Carbon Emissions?
summary: This paper examines the influence of the CEO–chairperson dialect connection on corporate carbon emissions. The results suggest that such a connection significantly increases corporate carbon emissions, and this effect is more pronounced amo
content: This paper examines the influence of the CEO–chairperson dialect connection on corporate carbon emissions. The results suggest that such a connection significantly increases corporate carbon emissions, and this effect is more pronounced among firms operating in highly competitive industries, non-state-owned enterprises and firms in non-heavily polluting industries. Further results show that this effect is stronger for firms with lower media coverage and for dialects that are more difficult for outsiders to understand. These findings indicate that the dialect connection increases corporate carbon emissions by weakening the monitoring effectiveness of chairpersons and by reinforcing cognitive preferences between CEOs and chairpersons. This study contributes to understanding how cultural factors shape corporate carbon emissions and suggests that informal linguistic ties can undermine corporate environmental accountability, revealing the dark side of informal connections among corporate leaders in capital markets.

title: The evolving role of climate commissions in the mi(d)st of unambitious UK climate policy, urban climate governance experimentation and place-based climate action
summary: Climate commissions have emerged across UK cities as new forms of urban climate governance experimentation, as national climate policy is marked by stagnation, political volatility, and a narrow focus on Net Zero. Drawing on a mixed-method
content: Climate commissions have emerged across UK cities as new forms of urban climate governance experimentation, as national climate policy is marked by stagnation, political volatility, and a narrow focus on Net Zero. Drawing on a mixed-method approach, this article examines how climate commissions advance urban climate experimentation through: (1) place-shaping and (2) facilitating more networked, inclusive and pluralistic engagement. Commissions can contribute to urban climate governance through place-shaping practices, knowledge exchange, and creating collaborative spaces between public, private, and third sectors. However, our findings reveal how their experimental potential is limited by constrained resources, uneven legitimacy, and the scalar dominance of national Net Zero policy discourse, which shapes local priorities and restricts opportunities for transformative, justice-oriented climate action. Rather than being fully autonomous sites of innovation, most commissions operate as hybrid governance intermediaries, supporting local authorities, translating national policy expectations, and cultivating context-specific climate responses. The ability of commissions to drive ambitious, equitable, and place-sensitive climate action depends on addressing structural and scalar constraints within the UK’s evolving climate policy regime. This article also contributes to wider urban theory, revealing how the governance innovation promise of such urban experiments also exposes and reproduces deeply embedded scalar, political, and institutional tensions.

title: Spatial Heterogeneity and Driving Mechanisms of Forest Carbon Storage in Wuyi Mountain National Park
summary: Forest aboveground live biomass carbon storage (hereafter referred to as “forest carbon storage”) is an important indicator of forest vegetation carbon sequestration, and its spatial patterns and associated factors are highly heterogeneous.
content: Forest aboveground live biomass carbon storage (hereafter referred to as “forest carbon storage”) is an important indicator of forest vegetation carbon sequestration, and its spatial patterns and associated factors are highly heterogeneous. Identifying these variations can improve the understanding of carbon accumulation in complex mountain forests and support fine-scale carbon assessment in similar ecosystems. The results showed the following. (1) The total forest carbon storage in the study area was 3.75 × 106 t C, with a carbon density of 44.83 t C·hm−2. Pinus massoniana and hard broad-leaved tree species were the main contributors, and carbon storage peaked at the mature forest stage. (2) Carbon storage exhibited significant spatial clustering (Moran’s I = 0.312), with high-value areas concentrated within the national nature reserve and low-value areas distributed in regions with frequent human activities. (3) The GWR model outperformed the ordinary least squares model, with R2 increasing to 0.88 and residual spatial autocorrelation reduced by 42.22%. (4) The positive effect of stand volume increased from northeast to southwest, the effect of stand age differed between eastern and western areas, and shrub layer height, soil depth, and slope exhibited region-specific positive and negative effects, with significant interactions among factors.

title: Lithography-Free Electrical Contact Method for Optoelectronic and Flexible Devices Based on Mechanically Exfoliated 2D Materials
summary: We report a tabletop, versatile and lithography-free electrical contacting method for two-dimensional (2D) materials and van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures based on silver paint micromanipulation (SPMM). Operated under an ambient optical
content: We report a tabletop, versatile and lithography-free electrical contacting method for two-dimensional (2D) materials and van der Waals (vdW) heterostructures based on silver paint micromanipulation (SPMM). Operated under an ambient optical microscope, this additive, room-temperature approach circumvents the chemical solvents and high temperatures associated with conventional cleanroom processing used in electrode fabrication. We validate the efficacy of this strategy by fabricating devices based on high-quality mechanically exfoliated thin flakes on both rigid SiO2/Si and flexible polycarbonate substrates. On rigid supports, SPMM-contact multilayer graphene devices exhibit linear Ohmic behavior with excellent environmental stability over multiple days and an ambipolar field effect. Gate-tunable multilayer graphene/few-layer MoS2/multilayer graphene field-effect transistors demonstrate n-type gating with a two-terminal carrier mobility of 60 cm2Vs and time-resolved photoresponse under 660 nm and 415 nm illumination, with responsivities as high as 10 A/W at the lowest incident powers.
