title: The FDI Attraction Effect of Green Supply Chain Certification: Evidence from RCEP Countries
summary: Against the backdrop of a sluggish global economic recovery, escalating geopolitical volatility, and increasingly urgent climate governance, the flow of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) by Multinational Enterprises (MNEs) is undergoing profo
content: Against the backdrop of a sluggish global economic recovery, escalating geopolitical volatility, and increasingly urgent climate governance, the flow of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) by Multinational Enterprises (MNEs) is undergoing profound structural reshaping. With the global green trade barriers, represented by the European Union's Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM), officially entering the definitive implementation and verification phase in 2026, the environmental compliance capacity of host countries has transitioned from a mere cost burden to a core novel determinant of capital flows. Grounded in the macro context of the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), this paper deeply integrates the institution-based view, the "Porter Hypothesis", and institutional decoupling theory to systematically analyze the underlying logic and micro-mechanisms of how Green Supply Chain (GSC) certification influences MNEs' FDI location choices. Based on panel data from 15 member countries spanning 2010 to 2022 and constructing a two-way fixed effects model, the empirical results reveal that GSC certification, represented by ISO 14001, significantly promotes FDI inflows. This finding not only confirms that environmental compliance has transformed from a "transaction cost" into an "institutional asset" with strategic premium, but also highlights the critical signaling role of voluntary environmental standards in reducing information asymmetry in cross-border transactions and evading "greenwashing" regulatory risks. This study expands the connotation of location advantages in the classic Ownership-Location-Internalization (OLI) paradigm. It not only provides scientific location coordinates for MNEs to navigate penetrative carbon verification and optimize Asia-Pacific supply chain layouts, but also offers forward-looking empirical evidence and strategic insights for developing RCEP members to abandon formalistic investment attraction strategies and formulate substantive macro-green economic transition policies.

title: FORM-TRACE: A formula-based method for tracking forest-management transitions at Harvard Forest from 1908 to 2026
summary: Long-term changes in forest management are documented across reports, plans, and scientific papers written for different purposes and with changing vocabularies. This makes it difficult to show how a documentary record was converted into a
content: Long-term changes in forest management are documented across reports, plans, and scientific papers written for different purposes and with changing vocabularies. This makes it difficult to show how a documentary record was converted into a temporal claim. FORM-TRACE is a formula-based workflow that records corpus decisions, extraction quality, domain terms, and calculations before interpretation. We demonstrate it with Harvard Forest and New England documents dated 1908–2026. Of 257 PDFs inspected, 215 met the analytical criteria; 201 were extracted and scored, 14 were flagged as unreadable, scanned, or corrupted, and 42 methods-support references were kept outside the scored corpus. The method provides: • a corpus manifest and extraction log that expose inclusion, exclusion, and coverage gaps; • a keyword-domain matrix and five numbered equations that produce document- and period-level indicators; • saved score tables, plot data, and validation records that allow independent checking without redistributing copyrighted PDFs. FORM-TRACE measures documented attention rather than management performance and keeps interpretation separate from scoring.

title: Coupling exogenous and endogenous forces in rural revitalization: a village-scale coordination diagnostic in Fujian, China
summary: This study addresses two persistent challenges in China's rural revitalization: difficulty in reading village development dynamics and reliance on homogeneous governance toolkits. We propose a New Endogenous-Coupling diagnostic lens transla
content: This study addresses two persistent challenges in China's rural revitalization: difficulty in reading village development dynamics and reliance on homogeneous governance toolkits. We propose a New Endogenous-Coupling diagnostic lens translating neo-endogenous development into village-scale measurement tools, conceptualizing development as interaction between exogenous enabling conditions and endogenous capacities. A village-scale diagnostic framework combines AHP weighting, subsystem efficacy scoring, and a coupling-coordination index across a holistic-dynamic-elemental logic. Applied to 22 villages in Changtai District, Fujian Province using multi-source planning, administrative, spatial data and field verification. Exogenous conditions exceed endogenous capacity in 12/22 villages; exogenous systems are production-oriented, while endogenous strengths concentrate in industry/resource activation, with weaker organizational and cultural capacities. Most villages are transitional-to-coordinated; however, balanced subsystem scores do not guarantee high coordination when both are constrained. Four governance types emerge: exogenous-led, endogenous-led, synchronous, and low-coordination villages. Policy toolbox supports capability conversion, targeted enabling, bottleneck adjustment, and triage, improving goal-instrument fit and reducing homogenized interventions.

title: Yürüme mesafesinde yaşam: 15 dakikalık şehir kavramı üzerine çok boyutlu bir derleme
summary: 15 dakikalık şehir modeli, bireylerin günlük yaşam gereksinimlerini yürüme veya bisiklet mesafesinde karşılayabileceği, erişilebilir, çok işlevli ve yaşanabilir mahalleler oluşturmayı amaçlayan çağdaş bir kent planlama yaklaşımıdır. Bu mode
content: 15 dakikalık şehir modeli, bireylerin günlük yaşam gereksinimlerini yürüme veya bisiklet mesafesinde karşılayabileceği, erişilebilir, çok işlevli ve yaşanabilir mahalleler oluşturmayı amaçlayan çağdaş bir kent planlama yaklaşımıdır. Bu model, sürdürülebilir ulaşımı desteklerken, mekansal yakınlık temelinde toplumsal eşitlik, çevresel sorumluluk ve yaşam kalitesi gibi çok boyutlu hedefleri de içermektedir. Ancak literatürde kavramın bu tematik boyutları arasında bütüncül bir sınıflandırma yaklaşımı geliştirilememiştir. Bu çalışma, Scopus veri tabanında yer alan ve 15 dakikalık şehir kavramına doğrudan atıfta bulunan 103 akademik yayını sistematik bir şekilde inceleyerek; yakınlık, algı, katılım ve politika olmak üzere dört boyut altında sınıflandırmaktadır. İçerik analizi yöntemiyle gerçekleştirilen bu tematik çözümlemede hem kavramsal hem de uygulamalı düzeyde literatürdeki eğilimler ve boşluklar ortaya koyulmaya çalışılmıştır. Çalışmanın ana bulgusu olarak 15 dakikalık şehir planlaması ve çalışmalarının daha çok yakınlık ve politika üzerine yoğunlaştığı, algı ve katılım boyutlarının yeterince ele alınmadığı ortaya konulmuştur.

title: Coalizões de poder e hegemonia narrativa na política de pagamento por serviços ambientais no Brasil
summary: Este artigo analisa o processo de formulação da Política Nacional de Pagamento por Serviços Ambientais (PNPSA), um marco legislativo abrangente que institucionalizou um sistema nacional de PSA no Brasil. Embora a PNPSA abranja estruturas de
content: Este artigo analisa o processo de formulação da Política Nacional de Pagamento por Serviços Ambientais (PNPSA), um marco legislativo abrangente que institucionalizou um sistema nacional de PSA no Brasil. Embora a PNPSA abranja estruturas de governança, mecanismos de financiamento e diretrizes de implementação, este artigo concentra sua análise na dimensão mais contestada da política: a elegibilidade de áreas de conservação legalmente obrigatórias — Áreas de Preservação Permanente (APPs), Reservas Legais e Áreas de Uso Restrito — para recebimento de pagamentos por serviços ambientais com recursos públicos. O estudo demonstra que a combinação de coalizões dominantes e narrativas hegemônicas produziu um resultado de política pública consistente com a captura institucional sob o discurso da sustentabilidade. Dois referenciais teóricos complementares são mobilizados: o Advocacy Coalition Framework (ACF), que examina como sistemas de crenças e o aprendizado orientado a políticas públicas estruturam coalizões de atores; e o Narrative Policy Framework (NPF), que investiga como as narrativas de política pública legitimam posições e constroem significados morais. Do ponto de vista metodológico, a pesquisa aplica análise de conteúdo qualitativa de documentos legislativos, transcrições de audiências públicas e reportagens jornalísticas, com suporte de triangulação de dados. Os resultados revelam a predominância de uma coalizão composta por representantes do agronegócio e atores aliados, que reinterpretou o conceito de “adicionalidade” e consolidou uma narrativa moral que legitima a compensação pela conservação legalmente obrigatória. A discussão evidencia que, embora a PNPSA seja institucionalmente inovadora, ela reforça padrões históricos de concentração de poder e representação desigual na governança ambiental brasileira

title: Energy Metals and ESG-Driven Sustainability Uncertainty: Insights From Time-Frequency-Quantile Analysis
summary: This study examines the causal link between ESG uncertainty and energy metals. Using monthly data from February 2009 to January 2024 and a Rolling Windows Wavelet Quantile Granger Causality framework, in its first application in this contex
content: This study examines the causal link between ESG uncertainty and energy metals. Using monthly data from February 2009 to January 2024 and a Rolling Windows Wavelet Quantile Granger Causality framework, in its first application in this context, we uncover consistent predictive linkages across horizons, frequencies, and quantiles. Results show that ESG uncertainty predicts energy metals across horizons, frequencies, and quantiles. Policymakers and investors should integrate these insights into forecasting and strategy.

title: Aligning Ghana’s Carbon Credit Regulation with International Climate Commitments: Legal Gaps and Institutional Imperatives
source: SOAS Research Online (SOAS University of London)
summary: Ghana’s Environmental Protection Act 2025 (Act 1124) establishes the ﬁrst statutory framework for carbon market participation in the country’s history. This comment argues that the Act creates a formally adequate but structurally incomplete
content: Ghana’s Environmental Protection Act 2025 (Act 1124) establishes the ﬁrst statutory framework for carbon market participation in the country’s history. This comment argues that the Act creates a formally adequate but structurally incomplete regime: it builds an international trading architecture on top of an unresolved property rights question generated by Ghana’s pluralist land tenure system. Approximately eighty per cent of Ghana’s land is held under customary tenure by stools and skins, yet the Act defers the deﬁnition of carbon rights and ownership to future regulations. This deferral is not a technical gap alone; it reﬂects a fundamental tension between the Article 6 market logic, which presupposes clear, state-authorised, tradeable entitlements, and the customary legal order in which land and resource rights are communally held and ﬁduciarily administered. Drawing on doctrinal analysis of Act 1124 and Ghana’s updated Nationally Determined Contribution (2021), this comment contends that durable carbon market governance in Ghana requires not merely supplementary regulations but a coherent mediation of two normative orders. Legal pluralism provides the analytical lens for this diagnosis and for the reform framework the article proposes.

title: Optimized Sowing Date and Seeding Rate for Simultaneous Improvement of Yield and Quality of Late-Sown Winter Wheat in the Southern North China Plain
summary: Sowing date and seeding rate are key agronomic measures for regulating yield formation and quality accumulation in winter wheat, especially in the context of global warming, which has led to delayed sowing becoming the norm. Clearly identif
content: Sowing date and seeding rate are key agronomic measures for regulating yield formation and quality accumulation in winter wheat, especially in the context of global warming, which has led to delayed sowing becoming the norm. Clearly identifying optimal combinations of sowing date and seeding rate under late-sowing conditions is crucial for achieving coordinated improvement in both high yield and quality. Therefore, this study used the strong-gluten wheat cultivar ‘Shaannong 33’ and conducted a two-factor split-plot field experiment in the southern North China Plain (Nanyang, Henan) during 2019–2021. Three sowing dates (early sowing: 27 October; intermediate sowing: 31 October–2 November; late sowing: 6–8 November) and four seeding rates (180 × 104, 240 × 104, 300 × 104, and 360 × 104 plants ha−1) were tested to systematically analyze the effects of sowing date and seeding rate on wheat yield and its components, grain processing quality, and starch physicochemical properties. The results showed that sowing from late October to early November (approximately 25 October to 2 November in 2019–2020 and 25 October to 31 October in 2020–2021) combined with a seeding rate of 240–300 × 104 plants ha−1 maintained yield at a comparably high level across both growing seasons while improving processing quality indicators such as protein content, wet gluten content, and dough stability time for the strong-gluten cultivar ‘Shaannong 33’. However, the optimal sowing window varied between years: in 2019–2020, both D1 (27 October) and D2 (2 November) produced comparable yields, whereas in 2020–2021, D2 (31 October) was superior for both yield and quality. This inter-annual variability highlights the influence of climatic conditions on the optimal sowing window. Further delaying the sowing date to after 6 November led to decreases in yield and quality parameters; however, increasing the seeding rate to 360 × 104 plants ha−1 partially compensated for yield loss. In addition, late sowing significantly increased amylopectin content, swelling power, and pasting indicators such as peak viscosity and final viscosity while decreasing amylose content and pasting temperature, which is beneficial for improving cooking and eating quality. Correlation analysis indicated that the amylose/amylopectin ratio was the core factor determining starch pasting properties, while protein content showed a significant negative correlation with starch pasting indicators, reflecting the resource competition effect between grain protein and starch. Yield differences between the two years were mainly driven by changes in spike number per unit area, while inter-annual climate fluctuations (especially precipitation and temperature) significantly affected spike formation capacity. Overall, sowing date and seeding rate have a synergistic regulatory effect on yield and quality of late-sown wheat for the strong-gluten cultivar ‘Shaannong 33’. It is recommended to adopt a sowing date of 25–31 October w

title: Civil additive manufacturing: foundations and frontiers of the modern construction industry
summary: Abstract Civil additive manufacturing represents a specialized subset of additive manufacturing technologies operating at the construction scale and governed by distinct material, process, and regulatory constraints. This study presents a t
content: Abstract Civil additive manufacturing represents a specialized subset of additive manufacturing technologies operating at the construction scale and governed by distinct material, process, and regulatory constraints. This study presents a taxonomy-driven narrative-conceptual review of Civil AM using peer-reviewed literature alongside select gray literature, including institutional reports, industry white papers, and documented construction demonstrations. Through comparative discussion of construction-scale materials, printing techniques, and deployment strategies, this article assesses conditional benefits and limitations of Civil AM relative to conventional construction practices, with emphasis on scalability, cost efficiency, sustainability, and structural performance. This review highlights the absence of AM-specific construction standards as a critical barrier to industrial adoption and regulatory approval, complicating safety assessment and life-cycle evaluation of 3D-printed structures. By integrating technological developments with performance considerations, life-cycle perspectives, and standardization challenges, this study provides a structured foundation for evaluating construction methods and outlines future research directions necessary for scalable, automated, and code-compliant construction.

title: Effects of Lactobacillus plantarum, Bacillus subtilis, and a compound protease on the nutritional value and anti-nutritional factors of fermented soybean meal
summary: This study evaluated the effects of Lactobacillus plantarum , Bacillus subtilis , and a compound protease on the nutritional value, protein fractions, amino acid composition, anti-nutritional factors, and small intestinal degradability of s
content: This study evaluated the effects of Lactobacillus plantarum , Bacillus subtilis , and a compound protease on the nutritional value, protein fractions, amino acid composition, anti-nutritional factors, and small intestinal degradability of soybean meal (SBM) during anaerobic fermentation. SBM was fermented for 7 days at 40% moisture under four treatments: no additive (CON), microbial inoculation (ML; Lactobacillus plantarum (4.5 × 10 7 CFU/g) + Bacillus subtilis (4.5 × 10 7 CFU/g)), protease addition (LE; 1% fresh weight), and combined microbial–protease treatment (MLLE; Lactobacillus plantarum (4.5 × 10 7 CFU/g) + Bacillus subtilis (4.5 × 10 7 CFU/g) + protease (1% fresh weight)). During fermentation, crude protein (CP) increased while neutral detergent fiber (NDF) and acid detergent fiber (ADF) decreased, with MLLE showing the greatest reduction. ML, LE, and MLLE significantly increased the non-protein nitrogen (PA) and rapidly degradable protein (PB1) fractions, with the greatest increases observed in LE, while LE and MLLE markedly reduced proteins >42 kDa. Amino acid dynamics differed among treatments: ML showed a ‘rise–fall’ pattern; in LE, amino acid levels increased steadily and stabilized by day 5, whereas in MLLE, they remained relatively stable. LE effectively reduced proteinaceous anti-nutritional factors (glycinin, β-conglycinin), ML decreased oligosaccharides (raffinose, stachyose), and MLLE reduced all types of anti-nutritional factors. Small intestinal degradability was significantly improved by all treatments, with MLLE achieving the greatest improvement. Improvements plateaued by day 3. In conclusion, anaerobic fermentation of SBM with Lactobacillus plantarum , Bacillus subtilis , and compound protease is an effective approach to enhance protein quality, reduce anti-nutritional factors, and improve intestinal degradability. Considering efficiency and cost-effectiveness, a fermentation duration of 3 days appears optimal.

title: Post-Harvest Handling and Food Security
summary: Postharvest handling and management of agricultural products are important for retarding rate of food deterioration, maintaining food quality, ensuring food safety, increasing food availability and accessibility, thereby promoting economic
content: Postharvest handling and management of agricultural products are important for retarding rate of food deterioration, maintaining food quality, ensuring food safety, increasing food availability and accessibility, thereby promoting economic stability and global food security. Postharvest handling measures include cleaning, sorting, grading, drying, packaging, storage management, transportation and marketing. Proper harvesting techniques and time help to maintain quality in fruits, vegetables and grains, while reducing physical damages that may stimulate decay by microorganisms along the food supply chain. Drying helps to reduce moisture content which reduces rate of enzymatic and microbial activities that stimulate spoilage in storageThe use of proper technology in postharvest handling has helped to significantly reduce postharvest losses in crops. Recent smart strategies and technological innovations in postharvest management of crops have the capacities to enhance global food security. The smart strategies include mechanized harvesting, automated cleaning and sorting techniques, use of safe and edible coatings with other effective botanical preparations, and use of biodegradable and reusable packaging materials in the transportation of agricultural produce. Many of these techniques reduce human interface with crops and protect them from postharvest pests. Latest technologies incorporate Internet of Things (IoT), smart sensors, artificial intelligence and solar-powered efficient systems in postharvest management of produce. Downscaled, multipurpose, user-friendly and cheaper technologies would be more accessible to farmers, with organizing trainings and demonstration to build their capacity in postharvest management to promote global food security. Investment in advances in postharvest technology across regions will enhance global food security.

title: Factores asociados a la participación femenina en la ganadería extensiva
summary: La participación equitativa de las mujeres en el sector agrario trasciende su dimensión social y se configura como un factor determinante para la generación de beneficios económicos, entre los que destacan el incremento de la productividad,
content: La participación equitativa de las mujeres en el sector agrario trasciende su dimensión social y se configura como un factor determinante para la generación de beneficios económicos, entre los que destacan el incremento de la productividad, la promoción del desarrollo sostenible, la diversificación de actividades y una mayor propensión a la innovación y la resiliencia. La presente investigación analiza la participación femenina en la ganadería en España, con especial atención a la ganadería extensiva, con el propósito de identificar las características asociadas y aportar evidencia que sustente políticas orientadas a su incorporación en un subsector en retroceso y con elevado valor ecosistémico. Las preguntas de investigación se centran en determinar el nivel de participación femenina en la ganadería, así como los factores que inciden en dicha participación. El estudio se apoya en dos fuentes principales: el Censo Agrario 2020 y el Mapa de Ganaderías Extensivas. Los resultados evidencian que la ganadería extensiva presenta condiciones favorables para la equidad, lo que refuerza su potencial dentro del desarrollo rural sostenible. Los modelos de regresión logística identifican como factores significativos la mayor edad, el tamaño de la explotación, la pertenencia a empresas familiares y la orientación productiva, con preferencia por ganado mayor en la ganadería general y por ganado menor en la extensiva. Estos hallazgos confirman la idoneidad de la ganadería extensiva para promover la igualdad y delinean líneas estratégicas para la formulación de políticas públicas. La participación femenina se perfila como un elemento clave para la resiliencia del sector, mientras que su incorporación tardía y con menor experiencia subraya la necesidad de eliminar barreras como la edad en la concesión de ayudas y garantizar programas de capacitación especializada.

title: AI-Driven Diagnostics and Predictive Modeling: Transforming Clinical Decision-Making in Modern Medicine
summary: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming clinical medicine from reactive intervention to predictive, data-driven care. This chapter examines how contemporary AI systems – ranging from convolutional and recurrent networks to transformers
content: Artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming clinical medicine from reactive intervention to predictive, data-driven care. This chapter examines how contemporary AI systems – ranging from convolutional and recurrent networks to transformers, graph neural networks, and large language models – are redefining diagnostics, predictive modeling, and clinical decision support. Diagnostic AI enhances precision across radiology, dermatology, pathology, and cardiology by detecting patterns beyond human perception, while predictive algorithms forecast clinical deterioration, treatment response, and population-level trends. The integration of AI into Clinical Decision Support Systems (CDSS) demonstrates how probabilistic reasoning can augment, rather than replace, clinician judgment. Emerging paradigms such as multimodal learning and digital twins extend AI’s capacity to simulate and personalize care, bridging data streams from imaging, genomics, and wearables. Alongside technical innovation, the chapter addresses essential ethical, regulatory, and societal dimensions – bias, transparency, accountability, and trust – that determine whether these tools advance equity or reinforce disparity. By synthesizing technological foundations, clinical applications, and governance frameworks, the chapter envisions a future of collaborative intelligence where human and artificial cognition converge to deliver medicine that is not only intelligent but humane.

title: Fermentation with commercial starters of whey from cheese made by artisanal producers as a solution to valorise this byproduct
summary: ABSTRACT Whey obtained from artisanal cheese production is a food by‑product with excellent nutritional characteristics, but managing it is often difficult and does not provide significant economic benefits. Our objective was to offer biote
content: ABSTRACT Whey obtained from artisanal cheese production is a food by‑product with excellent nutritional characteristics, but managing it is often difficult and does not provide significant economic benefits. Our objective was to offer biotechnological solutions, based on controlled fermentations with commercial starters, that enable the valorization of whey and its potential application for generating new fermented foods. Six commercial starters, two mesophilic and four thermophilic, were used to ferment cow’s cheese whey. It was observed that all the products obtained were microbiologically safe, as no pathogens were detected after four weeks of storage. Thermophilic starters were more efficient to achieve a fast acidification, accompanied by higher amount of lactic acid, and normally generated a higher abundance of volatile organic compounds, and were therefore considered more suitable for achieving our purpose. Among the thermophilic cultures tested, YC-350 was selected based on its rapid acidification and its favorable production of aroma-related metabolites. The selected starter was used to produce four products, two fermented and two unfermented, and two of them (one fermented and one unfermented) were supplemented with a blueberry extract that provided a fruity flavor. Sensory analysis showed that the two blueberry-supplemented drinks were preferred (scores of 3.3±0.8 and 3.1±0.9) among consumers, compared to the two whey products without supplementation (scores of 1.7±0.9 and 1.9±1.0). Furthermore, among highest rated, fermentation generated distinctive flavor and aroma attributes compared to simply combining unfermented whey with blueberry juice. Our results show that the starters available on-site can be used in small artisanal dairies to add value to the whey they generate and contribute to the implementation of more sustainable practices, promoting the circularity of the food chain.

title: PERFORMANCE AND ECONOMIC VIABILITY OF CHEMICAL FERTILIZER SUBSTITUTED WITH ANAEROBIC DIGESTION EFFLUENT ON RICE PRODUCTION
summary: A field experiment was conducted over a period of 123 days, spanning the rice (Oryza sativa L.) growth cycle from July to November 2023, to evaluate different ratios of chemical fertilizer reduction and anaerobic digestion effluent (ADE) su
content: A field experiment was conducted over a period of 123 days, spanning the rice (Oryza sativa L.) growth cycle from July to November 2023, to evaluate different ratios of chemical fertilizer reduction and anaerobic digestion effluent (ADE) substitution. Compared with chemical fertilizer at 100 % (T1), the chemical fertilizer at 50 % and ADE at 50 % (T3) treatment enhanced rice growth by increasing fresh weight, tiller numbers, soil plant analysis development (SPAD), and panicle. Chemical fertilizer at 75 % and ADE at 25 % (T2) and T3 treatment showed the positive effects on nutritional quality of rice grain through the higher levels of protein, amylose, amylopectin, amino acids, and trace elements. However, rice grain yields decreased by 5 and 6 % under T2 and T3, respectively, compared with T1. This reduction may be attributed to the slow-release characteristics of ADE. Therefore, multi‑year field trials are necessary to validate the long‑term sustainability of partial ADE substitution. The break-even point for the three scenarios was determined by harvesting and selling more than 60 % of the rice. Although lower grain yields resulted in reduced profits, the economic analysis indicated positive implications for partial substitution of chemical fertilizer with ADE. Thus, T3 treatment may represent a more sustainable option for long-term rice production. The findings of the present study provide valuable insights for recycling ADE as a renewable resource in agricultural production.

title: Effect of Packaging Method and Storage Time on Fatty Acid Profile and Oxidative Stability of Ground Beef Lipid Fraction During Refrigerated Storage
summary: This study evaluated the effect of packaging method and storage time on the fatty acid profile and lipid stability of ground beef during 21 days of storage (0–4 °C). Ground beef was packaged under vacuum (VP) and modified atmosphere packagi
content: This study evaluated the effect of packaging method and storage time on the fatty acid profile and lipid stability of ground beef during 21 days of storage (0–4 °C). Ground beef was packaged under vacuum (VP) and modified atmosphere packaging (MAP 80% O2/20% CO2 and MAP 50% O2/50% CO2). Lipid oxidation progressed during storage particularly in MAP 80/20 samples, where TBARS reached 3.46 mg MDA/kg of product after 21 days, compared with 0.45 mg MDA/kg of product in VP samples. Redness (a*) decreased in MAP samples but remained stable in VP. Acid value increased, reaching 4.35 mg KOH/g fat in VP and 3.62 mg KOH/g fat in MAP 50/50. Despite oxidative changes, the fatty acid profile remained relatively stable, with saturated fatty acids accounting for 52–56% and oleic acid (33.85–38.99%) being predominant. VP most effectively limited the formation of secondary lipid oxidation products, as reflected by lower TBARS values, whereas MAP promoted lipid peroxidation during storage. These findings highlight the combined impact of packaging method and storage duration on the quality and stability of ground beef.

title: Network dynamics of systemic losses and sustainable financial contagion in global financial systems with ESG integration
source: International Journal of Science and Research Archive
summary: This paper develops an integrated framework to investigate the network dynamics of systemic losses and sustainable financial contagion in global financial systems with ESG integration. The framework begins by constructing a global financial
content: This paper develops an integrated framework to investigate the network dynamics of systemic losses and sustainable financial contagion in global financial systems with ESG integration. The framework begins by constructing a global financial network based on inter-institutional interconnectedness and correlation structures, enabling the identification of key transmission channels of systemic risk. We analyze the evolution of network topology and systemic loss propagation under various stress scenarios, including market disruptions and liquidation shocks, to assess the resilience of the financial system over time. Furthermore, advanced machine learning techniques are employed to evaluate and predict abnormal volatility among systemically important financial institutions, enhancing the detection of emerging contagion risks. The study also examines the role of ESG integration in mitigating financial contagion and influencing the transmission of systemic losses across global markets. Empirical findings indicate that stronger and more diversified network connections improve the resilience of financial systems against systemic shocks, while higher ESG adoption contributes to reducing the intensity of risk spillovers and promotes financial stability. Overall, the results highlight the importance of incorporating ESG considerations into financial network analysis to support a more sustainable, resilient, and interconnected global financial system. The proposed framework offers a comprehensive approach for understanding systemic risk dynamics and evaluating sustainable financial contagion in an increasingly complex financial environment.

title: Manufacturing Development and Regional Socioeconomic Outcomes in the Context of Hungary’s Battery Industry Expansion
summary: This paper examines the association between regional manufacturing development intensity and socioeconomic outcomes in Hungary in the context of the country’s recent battery-industry expansion, using an EU27 NUTS2 benchmark panel over 2013–
content: This paper examines the association between regional manufacturing development intensity and socioeconomic outcomes in Hungary in the context of the country’s recent battery-industry expansion, using an EU27 NUTS2 benchmark panel over 2013–2022. Using a two-way fixed effects framework, it analyses employment, compensation per employee, and the tertiary employment share, while also testing the conditioning role of regional innovation capacity. The results show limited evidence of broad-based employment expansion, clearer wage upgrading, and no systematic upgrading in the tertiary employment share. Wage gains are stronger in regions with higher human capital and R&D effort, suggesting that innovation capacity strengthens the association between manufacturing development intensity and local wage outcomes. The findings suggest that manufacturing deepening in the context of Hungary’s battery-industry expansion is associated with real but uneven regional socioeconomic outcomes.

title: Deep Eutectic Solvents: A Comprehensive Landscape of Two Decades of Research, Emerging Frontiers, and Translational Challenges (2003–2025)
summary: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have undergone a remarkable transformation over the past two decades, evolving from a laboratory curiosity into one of the most actively investigated solvent platforms in green chemistry. Yet, despite this rapi
content: Deep eutectic solvents (DESs) have undergone a remarkable transformation over the past two decades, evolving from a laboratory curiosity into one of the most actively investigated solvent platforms in green chemistry. Yet, despite this rapid expansion, and although the field is well served by numerous topical reviews, it still lacks a corpus-wide, cross-disciplinary synthesis capable of guiding strategic research priorities, identifying critical knowledge gaps, and informing policy and industrial investment decisions. The present work addresses this need through a thorough analysis of global DES research from 2003 to 2025, based on a deduplicated corpus of 17,757 publications retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection and Scopus following PRISMA-adapted screening guidelines. The analysis maps temporal publication dynamics, geographic and institutional contributions, thematic evolution, journal landscape, component usage patterns, international collaboration networks, market projections, and alignment with the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals. The results document an exponential growth trajectory—from a single publication in 2004 to 3954 in 2025 (CAGR > 30%)—and reveal a clear thematic transition from early electrochemistry-dominated research toward extraction, pharmaceutical, and environmental applications, with machine-learning-assisted design and hydrophobic DES formulations emerging as the most dynamic current frontiers. China leads global output with 6819 publications (38.4%), while the United States and Malaysia achieve the highest citation-per-publication ratios among the leading nations (≈46.7 and ≈38.9, respectively, versus ≈27.6 for China), and Spain pairs a comparatively modest output with a high h-index, indicating that impact is large relative to volume. Type III DESs and NADESs collectively account for approximately 69% of the literature, with choline chloride present in 72% of reported formulations. The global DES market, valued at approximately USD 166 million in 2024, is projected to reach USD 370 million by 2030. Despite this progress, critical translational barriers persist: fewer than 0.3% of publications include techno-economic or life cycle assessment analysis, standardized characterization protocols remain absent, and toxicological datasets are systematically incomplete. This panoramic analysis is intended to serve as an evidence-based reference for researchers prioritizing future directions, for funding agencies assessing the maturity and needs of the field, and for industrial stakeholders evaluating the readiness of DES technologies for scale-up.
