summary: It has become clear that the most important asset in today's organizations is not technology‚ capital or infrastructure but people․ Organizations will have to invest lavishly in retention and motivation of employees․ This is especially so i
content: It has become clear that the most important asset in today's organizations is not technology‚ capital or infrastructure but people․ Organizations will have to invest lavishly in retention and motivation of employees․ This is especially so in fast-moving and intellectual capital-driven industries such as the renewable energy sector․ There are solar companies in other emerging markets such as Uzbekistan that are growing quickly and face their own human resource challenges and opportunities․ There is a shortage of highly skilled‚ motivated‚ flexible human resources in the renewable energy workforce․ The workforce generally has a high rate of turnover‚ low levels of employee engagement‚ and poor performance‚ though this is rarely solely due to financial issues․ Instead‚ it is a mixture of a range of work factors including interpersonal relationships‚ leadership style‚ stress‚ and emotional and physical wellbeing․

title: Integration of hydrogen production, storage, and optical properties of X2CaZnH6 (X = Li, Na, K): A DFT study
summary: The current study utilizes the ab-initio calculations to delve into the structural, electronic, mechanical, hydrogen storage, photocatalytic water splitting, and optical properties of hydride perovskites X 2 CaZnH 6 (X = Li, Na, K). The neg
content: The current study utilizes the ab-initio calculations to delve into the structural, electronic, mechanical, hydrogen storage, photocatalytic water splitting, and optical properties of hydride perovskites X 2 CaZnH 6 (X = Li, Na, K). The negative formation enthalpy Δ H f (−2.81, −2.85, −2.76 eV/atom) and Goldschmidt tolerance factors ( t = 0.84, 0.91, 0.97) for X 2 CaZnH 6 (X = Li, Na, K) implies that these system are chemically stable with remarkable cubic phase. The thermodynamical stabilities are confirmed via well-known molecular dynamic simulation (AMID) based on Newtons law of energy conservation. These hydrides X 2 CaZnH 6 (X = Li, Na, K) reveals an indirect bandgaps of 1.93, 2.0, and 2.51 eV which are crucial for photocatalytic activities for water splitting. To performs these photocatalytic activities the values of band-edge potentials E V B (1.57, 1.55, 1.64 eV) and E C B (−1.35, −0.44, −0.85 eV) are calculated for X 2 CaZnH 6 (X = Li, Na, K) which highlights that these material suitable for water-splitting as X 2 CaZnH 6 fulfill the upper H ∗ /H 2 and lower limit O 2 /H 2 O of V vs. NHE (pH=0). Furthermore, the gravimetric ratio (C w t % ) of these X 2 CaZnH 6 (X = Li, Na, K) are also calculated as 4.75, 4.52, and 4.18 wt%, respectively. The storage capacity (C w t % ) values closely aligns with (US-DOE) target. In order, to check the practical feasibility of dehydrogenation the desorption temperature T d e s is computed as 477.17, 499.38, and 446.50 K for these X 2 CaZnH 6 (X = Li, Na, K). Additionally, a diverse nature of the dielectric constant ϵ ( ω ), suggests that these are potential materials for clean and renewable energy applications.

title: Embrace the Frizz: Use of Human Hair for Triboelectric Interactive Textiles
summary: Abstract This demo showcases the use of human hair as a triboelectric material for interactive textile sensing. It presents an interdisciplinary exploration of how a familiar biological material can be integrated into soft electronic system
content: Abstract This demo showcases the use of human hair as a triboelectric material for interactive textile sensing. It presents an interdisciplinary exploration of how a familiar biological material can be integrated into soft electronic systems to support more sustainable resource use while presenting sensorially engaging interactions with textile interfaces. The work is based on the principle of triboelectricity. Human hair is highly tribopositive and, when in contact with a tribonegative material, acquires a positive charge, typically experienced as static electricity and commonly known as hair frizz. While this phenomenon has been studied in other domains, such as the haircare industry, its potential remains underexplored within electronic textiles, biodesign, and interaction design. Building on this, this demo explores the use of human hair as a material for interactive textiles. As a renewable, biodegradable resource typically discarded as waste, hair offers a promising alternative to metals and toxic materials commonly used in traditional electronic textiles. In addition, it emphasises hair’s sensorial properties and its potential for interaction, drawing on shared understandings of what hair is and how it is touched, handled, and engaged with. Specifically, the demo features an interactive textile-based object in the form of a pillow, along with textile samples. Participants are invited to touch, press, and stroke the pillow, generating electrical peaks that are displayed in real time. Through this interaction, the audience can explore how different gestures and pressure patterns influence electricity generation. The demo aims to introduce audiences to new material constructions and design possibilities for interactive textiles. This biodesign approach bridges technical experimentation with the intimate dimension of working with a human-grown biomaterial, proposing hair-based electronic textiles as a pathway towards potentially more meaningful and sustainable soft interfaces.

title: Performance comparison of thermal storage and release of coaxial closed-loop geothermal system with different well configurations
summary: Abstract The issues of curtailment of renewable energy have become key bottlenecks restricting the large-scale development of renewable energy. Based on the coaxial closed-loop geothermal system and geological energy storage, this study con
content: Abstract The issues of curtailment of renewable energy have become key bottlenecks restricting the large-scale development of renewable energy. Based on the coaxial closed-loop geothermal system and geological energy storage, this study constructed vertical, L-shaped, and inverted T-shaped well. Numerical simulation was used to explore the effects of different well types and operation modes on heat storage and extraction performance as well as the evolution law of formation temperature, while the economic and environmental benefits under various scenarios were quantitatively evaluated. The results show that increasing the number of horizontal side wells can effectively raise the outlet temperature by 10–16 K. The inverted T-shaped well has the highest heat release power but the lowest heat storage power, which is the opposite of the vertical well. The introduction of the heat storage stage brings about higher heat release power and a longer service life of the formation, and the increase in horizontal side wells improves the stability of heat release power. Under the condition of low energy storage temperature, the inverted T-shaped well achieves the highest economic and environmental benefits, whereas the vertical well demonstrates more prominent growth rates of economic and environmental benefits between the two operation modes.

title: Accountability in Green Waqf Management in Support of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs): A Study of Miftahul Ulum Islamic Boarding School
summary: This study aims to analyze the accountability of green waqf management at Miftahul Ulum Islamic Boarding School from the perspective of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The study is motivated by the importance of strengthening acco
content: This study aims to analyze the accountability of green waqf management at Miftahul Ulum Islamic Boarding School from the perspective of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). The study is motivated by the importance of strengthening accountability to achieve transparent, professional, and sustainable waqf governance. This research employed a qualitative method with a case study approach through in-depth interviews, observations, and documentation involving waqf administrators at the Islamic boarding school. The findings reveal that the implementation of green waqf at Miftahul Ulum Islamic Boarding School contributes significantly to the achievement of the SDGs, particularly No Poverty (SDGs 1), Zero Hunger (SDGs 2), Quality Education (SDGs 4), and Clean Water and Sanitation (SDGs 6). However, the accountability system remains traditional and centered on the Kiai as the highest authority, with accountability mechanisms that are largely internal and trust-based. Limited formal documentation, written reporting, and asset legalization remain major challenges in establishing professional and modern waqf governance. This study recommends strengthening the capacity of nadzir, implementing digital reporting systems, and enhancing collaboration with relevant institutions to integrate sharia accountability principles and environmental sustainability in the management of green waqf in Islamic boarding schools.

title: How RENURE is shaping sustainable nitrogen management in the EU
summary: How RENURE is shaping sustainable nitrogen management in the EU Learn how the RENURE project is driving nutrient circularity in EU agriculture, offering a sustainable alternative to mineral fertilisers. The European Union is characterised b
content: How RENURE is shaping sustainable nitrogen management in the EU Learn how the RENURE project is driving nutrient circularity in EU agriculture, offering a sustainable alternative to mineral fertilisers. The European Union is characterised by regional disparities. Certain areas with high livestock densities, such as Flanders in Belgium and the Netherlands, are struggling with chronic nutrient surpluses, while other arable regions lack nutrients to meet crop needs. Paradoxically, European agriculture remains heavily dependent on (synthetic) mineral fertilisers. These nitrogen fertilisers are either imported or produced via the energy-intensive Haber-Bosch process, which consumes substantial amounts of natural gas. On top of that, the Farm to Fork strategy requires a 20% reduction in the use of synthetic fertilisers in agriculture by 2030.

title: AI-Driven Multi-Objective Optimization of Floating Photovoltaic-Thermal Systems with MATLAB-HOMER Pro Validation
source: International Journal of Computer Science and Engineering
summary: The shift towards renewable energy has increased interest in Floating Photovoltaic Thermal (FPVT) systems for their capacity to produce electricity and heat with a low land footprint. However, improvement of the FPV T scheme is difficult du
content: The shift towards renewable energy has increased interest in Floating Photovoltaic Thermal (FPVT) systems for their capacity to produce electricity and heat with a low land footprint. However, improvement of the FPV T scheme is difficult due to the multi-dimensional relationship between the electrical, thermal, and economic aspects. This research introduces an Artificial Intelligence (AI)-based multi-objective optimization and techno-economic analysis approach for FPV T systems based on ANN, GA, PSO, and RL System models. ANN surrogate predictors and optimization algorithms were implemented in MATLAB. The outcome of simulation results at STC yielded an active power and thermal output of 64.8 kW and 260 kW, respectively, resulting in a useful energy output of 324.8 kW. The conventional PV baseline system, however, produced 56.2 kW of output, at 15.3% gain in performance, higher than 480% gain in total energy utilization with the addition of the thermal recovery. The ANN predictor was highly accurate with an error of less than 0.01%, and the GA and PSO algorithms produced consistent optimal results. The reinforcement learning algorithm effectively controlled the flow rate of the coolant to achieve the desired outlet temperatures. The findings showed that a hybrid AI approach enhances electrical and thermal efficiency, speeds up the optimization process with surrogate modeling, and recommends low LCOE and attractive NPC configurations. The techno-economic modeling with HOMER Pro also validates the AI-optimized solutions. This technology advances renewable energy research through the use of multi-objective optimization, surrogate modeling, and techno-economic validation.

title: A REPORT ON THE GEOARCHAEOLOGICAL DEPOSIT MODELLING ON LAND AT THE TEESIDE RENEWABLE ENERGY PLANT SITE
summary: This report summarises the findings arising out of the geoarchaeological deposit modelling undertaken by Quaternary Scientific (University of Reading) in connection with the proposed development at the Tees Renewable Energy Plant Site (Nati
content: This report summarises the findings arising out of the geoarchaeological deposit modelling undertaken by Quaternary Scientific (University of Reading) in connection with the proposed development at the Tees Renewable Energy Plant Site (National Grid Reference: centred on NZ 54280 23180; Figure 1). During recent geotechnical investigations carried out by RPS Planning & Development, a total of eight boreholes and sixteen test-pits were put down across the site. The main aim of the geoarchaeological deposit modelling exercise is to reconstruct the sub-surface stratigraphy and environs of the site, and in particular to identify (1) any organic-rich horizons (e.g. peat) which may be suitable for further environmental archaeological investigations, (2) the original topography of the site and (3) the nature of the reclamation process. In order to accomplish these aims, the following objectives were formulated: (1) To carry out a systematic desk-based review of the new RPS geotechnical records put down across the site (2) To carry out a systematic and detailed review of previous British Geological Society (BGS) records nearby to the site (3) To produce 2-Dimensional models of the surfaces and thicknesses of the main stratigraphic units across the site (4) To provide recommendations for further work (if necessary) Eight geotechnical boreholes (<12m from surface) and sixteen test-pits (<4m from surface) were put down across the site by RPS Planning & Development. The thickness of Made Ground exceeded 4m rendering the test-pit records unusable within this geoarchaeological investigation. Similarly, the nature of the Made Ground meant that multiple attempts were required at some of the borehole locations (e.g. BH04 & BH07). The spatial co-ordinates of each borehole were not recorded, but have been estimated using georeferencing software and recent topographic surveys of the site (Table 1; Figure 1). Each borehole was described by the geotechnical team undertaking the drilling, the results of which are recorded in Tables 2 to 9. In addition, two borehole transects were produced orientated approximately north-south and west-east across the site (Figures 2 & 3). The borehole records indicate that in the northern and central areas of the site, the Made Ground tends to range between 5 and 8m in thickness and extends down to between ca. -0.50m and -1.00m OD (Figures 2 & 3). This level may be representative of the natural topography of the site prior to reclamation. However, it is also possible that in some places this former surface has been truncated during or prior to the reclamation process. In Borehole BH04, for example, towards the south of the site, the base of the Made Ground is at the lower level of -2.10m OD. title: Case Studies of Energy Transition Cases
summary: Chapter 11 is written by Filip Balcerzak and is titled “Case Studies of Energy Transition Cases”. The author provides a case study of energy transition cases, starting from observing that almost 27% of all publicly available investor–State
content: Chapter 11 is written by Filip Balcerzak and is titled “Case Studies of Energy Transition Cases”. The author provides a case study of energy transition cases, starting from observing that almost 27% of all publicly available investor–State arbitrations relate to the energy sector. The author notes that this makes the energy sector the most relevant economic sector for ISDS. The author notes that it is against this reality that the negative public perception that investor–State dispute settlement (ISDS) serves as an obstacle to energy transition and to the fight against climate change is rooted. This chapter expertly discusses the relevance of ISDS in energy transition by looking at various energy sectors – i.e. renewable, nuclear, and fossil fuels. The author does so primarily by a thorough and rich analysis of when and to what extent host States have relied on ‘environmental-based defenses’ during ISDS matters. The chapter analyses the renewable energy ISDS matters by investigating the developments in various States vis-à-vis regulatory changes in the energy sector – e.g. in Spain, Germany, the Czech Republic, Romania, Honduras, Italy, etc. The chapter illustrates the issues by real-life examples from the ISDS shop floor, looking at the issues with, inter alia , coal phase-outs, clawback of feed-in tariffs, revoking licenses, etc. The author concludes that international investment treaties do not constitute an obstacle to energy transition. As pertains to renewable energy investments, the author underscores the obvious fact that critiques often seem to forget, namely, that ‘the cases within this group result from disputes concerning investments without which energy transition would be impossible’. As regards ISDS in nuclear and fossil fuel, the author notes that there may indeed be a perception that it serves as an obstacle to the energy transition process. Meanwhile, the author notes that, to date, there has not been a single ISDS case in which restitution has been awarded. Thus, the real question is: ‘who should bear the financial burden of the energy transition?’ The answer to this question is heavily fact dependent, including considerations of legitimate State defenses rooted in energy transition law.

title: Low uptake of biodiversity friendly agricultural practices in steppe bird diversity hotspots
summary: Steppe birds are among the most endangered bird groups in Europe, primarily due to the intensification of agricultural activities. Spain is a key European stronghold for steppe birds, where many declining species currently live outside prot
content: Steppe birds are among the most endangered bird groups in Europe, primarily due to the intensification of agricultural activities. Spain is a key European stronghold for steppe birds, where many declining species currently live outside protected areas. The 2023–2027 Spanish CAP Strategic Plan (PEPAC) includes eco-schemes and rural development agri-environmental measures aimed at curbing farmland bird declines, with a particular focus on steppe birds. Here we assess whether PEPAC conservation measures are implemented effectively on areas of high conservation value for steppe birds. To this end, we evaluated the degree of spatial alignment between areas of high steppe bird diversity (hotspots) and the adoption of PEPAC measures. Steppe bird hotspots were selected based on the combined taxonomic, functional, and phylogenetic diversity of 26 steppe bird species in peninsular Spain. Uptake of the ‘Biodiversity Areas’ eco-scheme and the ‘Protection of Birds’ rural development measures were taken from official sources. Uptake was significantly higher in steppe bird hotspots than in non-hotspot areas, within land covers suitable for steppe birds (17.3 ± 14.1% vs 7.2 ± 10.8% for the eco-scheme and 0.8 ± 4.2% vs 0.3 ± 2.9% for the rural development measures, respectively; mean ± SD). Overall uptake was very low and well below the 30% target of the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. Results highlight an urgent need for more effective strategies to engage farmers and drive the adoption of biodiversity-oriented initiatives, using existing biodiversity maps and spatial analysis to guide CAP planning to safeguard key steppe bird areas.

title: Role of Sodium Acetate Anhydrate in the Nucleation of the Sodium Acetate Trihydrate Phase-Change Material
summary: High Resolution Image Download MS PowerPoint Slide Sodium acetate trihydrate (SAT) is a widely used phase-change material for thermal energy storage, but its tendency to supercool requires the use of nucleating agents to ensure reliable cry
content: High Resolution Image Download MS PowerPoint Slide Sodium acetate trihydrate (SAT) is a widely used phase-change material for thermal energy storage, but its tendency to supercool requires the use of nucleating agents to ensure reliable crystallization during operation. Upon heating, SAT undergoes peritectic decomposition to form a liquid phase and sodium acetate anhydrate (SAA). In this study, the role of SAA in the nucleation of SAT was investigated in detail. Two forms of SAA were compared: SAA-1, obtained by peritectic decomposition of SAT, and SAA-2, produced by thermal dehydration of SAT. Consistent with previous findings, SAA-1 was found to be inactive as a nucleating agent. Surprisingly, SAA-2 promoted reproducible crystallization of SAT over multiple heating–cooling cycles. Yet, the nucleation activity of SAA-2 gradually decreased during thermal cycling and was lost rapidly at elevated temperatures. Structural characterization with X-ray diffraction revealed that both SAA materials consist predominantly of the same polymorphs and they also displayed very similar Raman spectra. In contrast, pronounced differences in crystal morphology were observed in optical microscopy. SAA-1 forms large, well-faceted lath-shaped crystals, whereas SAA-2 consists of smaller, irregular crystallites with a high density of surface defects. These results indicate that SAT nucleation is controlled by the crystal morphology and surface structure of SAA, and that dissolution–recrystallization processes gradually convert the active SAA-2 into SAA-1 during thermal cycling, thereby eliminating its ability to nucleate SAT. More generally, the findings demonstrate that the performance of nucleating agents can be governed by the evolution and “healing” of their surface structures during operation, an aspect that should be considered in the design of durable phase-change materials for thermal energy storage.

title: Redefining Stability in Cultural Heritage Through Polymer Design: From Conservation Strategies to Plastic Degradation
summary: Polymers play a central and multifaceted role in cultural heritage science, serving both as functional materials in conservation treatments, such as cleaning, consolidation, adhesion and protection, and as constituents of a wide range of hi
content: Polymers play a central and multifaceted role in cultural heritage science, serving both as functional materials in conservation treatments, such as cleaning, consolidation, adhesion and protection, and as constituents of a wide range of historical artefacts, including paper and canvas, waterlogged wooden wrecks, musical instruments, and modern plastics used in art. Although numerous studies have examined the use of polymers in archaeology and cultural heritage conservation, most have focused on specific polymers, individual conservation treatments, or categories of artefacts. A comprehensive and integrated assessment of the multifunctional role of polymers, both as conservation materials and as constituents of heritage objects, remains lacking. The aim of this review is to provide a critical and comprehensive overview of natural and synthetic polymers in cultural heritage science, examining their applications in conservation treatments, their long-term stability and aging, and the challenges and opportunities associated with their preservation and sustainable use. This review examines the main classes of natural and synthetic polymers used in conservation, evaluating their mechanisms of action, performance, limitations, and long-term behavior across different applications. It also examines the chemical decomposition pathways and the resulting degradation phenomena occurring in polymeric materials, both as conservation products and as constituents of cultural artefacts, together with current stabilization strategies aimed at mitigating aging and deterioration. This review provides a critical appraisal of current challenges and future perspectives in cultural heritage conservation, highlighting emerging trends and research directions for the development of more effective, sustainable, and compatible polymer-based solutions for cultural heritage conservation.

title: Statcom'un Farkli Tipte Ve Dinamik Yüklerde Şebekedeki Etkilerinin Analizi
source: Journal of Scientific Technology and Engineering Research
summary: Bu çalışma, dinamik yük değişimlerinin yoğun olduğu güç sistemlerinde Statik Senkron Kompanzatör (STATCOM) ünitesinin gerilim regülasyonu ve reaktif güç kompanzasyonu performansını analiz ederek sistem kararlılığını incelemektedir. Bu doğru
content: Bu çalışma, dinamik yük değişimlerinin yoğun olduğu güç sistemlerinde Statik Senkron Kompanzatör (STATCOM) ünitesinin gerilim regülasyonu ve reaktif güç kompanzasyonu performansını analiz ederek sistem kararlılığını incelemektedir. Bu doğrultuda çalışmanın temel amacı; modern şebekelerde iletilen enerjinin kalitesini artırmak ve sistemin kararlı bir şekilde çalışmasını sağlamaktır. Esnek Alternatif Akım İletim Sistemleri (FACTS-Flexible AC Transmission Systems) tabanlı cihazlar, şebekede dinamik gerilim düzenlemesi yaparak güç faktörünün iyileştirilmesinde kritik rol oynamaktadır. STATCOM, FACTS gurubunda yaygın kullanılan şönt bileşenlerinden biridir. Şebekeye paralel olarak bağlanan bu cihaz, çalışma prensibi gereği bağlı olduğu sisteme sürekli olarak hem endüktif hem de kapasitif reaktif güç sağlayabilmekte veya ihtiyaç durumunda reaktif gücü absorbe eder. STATCOM; hızlı yanıt süresi, gerilim çökmeleri (SAG), harmonik distorsiyonlar ve ani yük değişimleri sırasında nominal akım kapasitesini düşük gerilim seviyelerinde dahi koruyabilme yeteneği ile öne çıkmaktadır. Bu dinamik karakteristik durum, cihazın modern güç sistemlerindeki kararlılığını sağlamaktadır. Sistemin kontrol mekanizmasında, Proportional-Integral (PI) kontrol yöntemi tercih edilmiştir. PI denetleyicinin yapısının sade olması, kolay uygulanabilirliği ve geniş bir lineer çalışma alanına sahip olması tercih nedenidir. Ayrıca, PI kontrolörlerin şebekedeki gerilim değişimlerine hızlı müdahale etmesi, regülasyon performansını artırmaktadır. Bu çalışma, MATLAB/Simulink ortamında modellenmiş ve elde edilen veriler simülasyon çıktıları ile desteklenmiştir. Analiz kapsamında, değişken yük koşulları altında STATCOM ’un güç faktörünü düzeltme performansı ve gerilim kararlılığı üzerindeki dinamik etkisi detaylı bir şekilde ele alınmıştır.

title: The ‘Modernised’ Energy Charter Treaty
summary: Chapter 10 is written by Ylli Dautaj and Lei Chen and is titled “The ‘Modernised’ Energy Charter Treaty: The Bridge and the Pathway Forward”. The authors start from the presumption that there is an imminent need for reforming the economy to
content: Chapter 10 is written by Ylli Dautaj and Lei Chen and is titled “The ‘Modernised’ Energy Charter Treaty: The Bridge and the Pathway Forward”. The authors start from the presumption that there is an imminent need for reforming the economy to make it ‘greener’. This chapter analyses the role that the Energy Charter Treaty (ECT) plays in this regard by promoting and protecting energy investments, including renewable ones. The authors discuss the ‘modernisation’ process of the treaty and whether and why it should be approved by its current and future member States. The authors explore whether the ECT – in its previous or modernised version – facilitates or obstructs energy transition. The authors entertain such analysis by explaining the inner workings of the ECT, including why it was implemented, how, and what achievements it has to date (including by looking at empirical data). The authors look at both the economic argument in favour of the ECT, as well as the policy argument. Finally, the authors analyse and explain the modernisation work and the product that leaves us with four major reforms/amendments to the ECT, namely, (1) jurisdictional amendments, (2) investment protection amendments, (3) sustainable development amendments, and (4) procedural amendments. The authors explain that if the modernised version enters into force, it will be a modern treaty that complies with sustainable development demands from a 21st-century citizenry. Conversely, if it does not – the old generation ECT will protect energy investments for the duration of the 20-year ‘sunset clause’. Finally, while the European Union may leave the ECT, the authors explain that it may turn into a global charter with countries from Africa and Asia joining. The central thesis of the chapter is that more multilateralism in the energy sector would be a good thing, and preferably through the modernised ECT.

title: First report on the chemical profile and antioxidant activity of Moroccan Crithmum maritimum essential oils
summary: Sea fennel (Crithmum maritimum L.) is a wild halophyte valued for its culinary, medicinal, and cosmetic applications owing to its rich nutritional profile and distinctive sensory properties. This study provides the first investigation of es
content: Sea fennel (Crithmum maritimum L.) is a wild halophyte valued for its culinary, medicinal, and cosmetic applications owing to its rich nutritional profile and distinctive sensory properties. This study provides the first investigation of essential oils (EOs) extracted from different parts of Moroccan C. maritimum (leaves, inflorescences, and stems) using hydrodistillation, with the aim of evaluating their phytochemical composition and bioactive potential. The oils were characterized by gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), while total phenolic content (TPC) and antioxidant activity (DPPH and FRAP assays) were assessed spectrophotometrically. The highest EO yield was obtained from inflorescences (0.59%), followed by leaves (0.44%) and stems (0.28%). GC-MS analysis identified more than 30 compounds, with dillapiole (16.41-32.47%), γ-terpinene (18.31-32.34%), and thymol methyl ether (19.76-22.33%) as the major constituents. Stems and leaves exhibited the highest phenolic contents (17.97 ± 1.07 and 17.64 ± 0.75 mg GAE/g EO, respectively), while inflorescences contained significantly lower amounts (15.17 ± 0.09 mg GAE/g EO). Antioxidant evaluation showed that leaf oil possessed the highest radical-scavenging capacity (DPPH), whereas stem oil demonstrated the greatest reducing power (FRAP). Molecular docking calculations were conducted to model the interaction between the six major constituents of C. maritimum EOs (dillapiole, γ-terpinene, thymol methyl ether, p-cymene, β-terpinene, and terpinen-4-ol), to evaluate their potential antioxidant activity. Among the identified C. maritimum EOs compounds, thymol methyl ether exhibited the most favorable binding profile with both target proteins NAD(P)H oxidase (PDB ID: 2CDU) and nitric oxide synthase (PDB ID: 6NGI), highlighting its potential as a broad-spectrum antioxidant. Overall, despite organ-dependent variations in yield and composition, all Moroccan C. maritimum EOs were rich in bioactive compounds with recognized biological properties. These findings highlight their potential for sustainable applications in nutraceutical, cosmetic, and food industries, supporting future valorisation of this halophyte through eco-friendly processing technologies.

title: Double Integral Sliding Mode Controller for Tracking Maximum Power in a Wind Turbine
source: Istanbul University - Journal of Electrical & Electronics Engineering
summary: Wind is a potential source of sustainable energy. But its inherent variability makes control issues critical for traditional control approaches. Herein, two nonlinear maximum power point trackers—sliding mode controller (SMC) and double int
content: Wind is a potential source of sustainable energy. But its inherent variability makes control issues critical for traditional control approaches. Herein, two nonlinear maximum power point trackers—sliding mode controller (SMC) and double integral sliding mode controller (DISMC)—are optimally designed to effectively track the maximum power in the below-rated wind speeds. A standard 4.8 MW wind turbine is analyzed using realistic wind variations in the MATLAB/Simulink software. Maximum power point tracker (MPPT) sets the speed reference from the error manifold of the turbine rotor angular velocity. Modifying the switching on the sliding surface to minimize chatter is also recommended here. The equilibrium optimizer adjusts the switching control to design an effective controller in the sliding plane. Monte Carlo simulations indicate that the normalized sum of square error for DISMC MPPT is 14.01% lower than the adaptive controller and 29.53% lower than the SMC, irrespective of internal uncertainty and disturbances. The Lyapunov stability of the proposed DISMC controller is verified, and its real-time implementation is ascertained in OPAL-RT with a marginal deviation of 0.5% from simulation. Cite this article as: S. Sahu, S. Behera and N. C. Giri, "Double integral sliding mode controller for tracking maximum power in a wind turbine," Electrica, 26, 0124, 2026. doi: 10.5152/electrica.2026.25124

title: AI-driven metaheuristic optimization for enhanced grid resilience under extreme weather and load shedding constraints
source: Journal of Electrical Systems and Information Technology
summary: Abstract The incorporation of Distributed Energy Resources (DER), especially PV and BESS, is essential in making radial power systems stable. Unfortunately, most recent optimization algorithms make an assumption of an unconstrained utility
content: Abstract The incorporation of Distributed Energy Resources (DER), especially PV and BESS, is essential in making radial power systems stable. Unfortunately, most recent optimization algorithms make an assumption of an unconstrained utility supply, targeting minimization of losses during daylight or only profit-making energy trading. Such traditional methods will not work in underdeveloped areas that face significant capacity limitations in their main substations, forcing them to undertake mandatory load shedding. In such situations, having an unconstrained BESS leads to parasitic voltage drop at weak tail nodes, whereas reactive disconnect switches lead to excessive Energy Not Served (ENS) production. In order to fill this gap, an artificial intelligence-based approach of survivability control that changes the focus from economic dispatching to active grid survivability has been proposed in this study. By using Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), the proposed approach incorporates modelling of artificial solar intermittency, constrained and asymmetric dispatching of BESS systems, and a demand-side management procedure. A penalization technique is used to ensure strict adherence to the statutory voltage constraints. Using the IEEE 33 bus network system with the maximum capacity for active power at 4.0 MW, the AI-based approach performed significantly better compared to the conventional distributed generation strategies. The new proposed approach was able to ensure that there were no violations of the absolute minimum network voltage (0.95 p.u.), reduced power losses to 1.696 MWh (a 31.6% improvement over static DG methodologies), and prevented all instances of unexpected Energy Not Served (ENS).

title: ANN-based surrogate modeling of composite laminates for structural optimization of wave energy converters
summary: Wave energy converters (WECs) possess considerable renewable energy potential; however, their large-scale deployment remains constrained by structural durability limitations and high manufacturing costs in harsh marine environments. Composi
content: Wave energy converters (WECs) possess considerable renewable energy potential; however, their large-scale deployment remains constrained by structural durability limitations and high manufacturing costs in harsh marine environments. Composite materials offer favorable strength-to-weight characteristics, yet optimizing laminate configurations via conventional finite element analysis (FEA) is computationally intensive, limiting exploration of high-dimensional design spaces. This study proposes a surrogate-based structural optimization framework integrating high-fidelity FEA with machine learning for composite WEC buoy design. A parametric analysis of a truncated spheroidal buoy was performed in ANSYS, systematically varying material type, stacking sequence, ply orientation, and laminate thickness under wave loading to construct a structural response database. An artificial neural network, trained on this dataset (R² = 0.97, RMSE = 1.8 mm) and coupled with a genetic algorithm, identified Pareto-optimal laminate configurations minimizing deformation subject to mass constraints. Optimized designs, validated against independent FEA simulations, exhibited deviations below 5%, substantially reducing computational cost and enabling scalable composite WEC hull design.

title: Stakeholder Engagement and Sustainability of the Blue Economy in Mombasa and Lamu Counties, Kenya
summary: This study examined the effects of stakeholder engagement on the sustainability of the blue economy in Mombasa and Lamu Counties, Kenya. The study was anchored on Common-Pool Resources (CPR) Theory. A pragmatic research philosophy and a con
content: This study examined the effects of stakeholder engagement on the sustainability of the blue economy in Mombasa and Lamu Counties, Kenya. The study was anchored on Common-Pool Resources (CPR) Theory. A pragmatic research philosophy and a convergent mixed-methods design were adopted. The study targeted 1,881 stakeholders across government agencies, local communities, NGOs, and the private sector, from whom a sample of 330 respondents was selected using purposive and simple random sampling. Data were collected using semi-structured questionnaires and interview guides and analyzed using descriptive statistics, correlation and regression analyses, and thematic analysis. The findings revealed a strong positive and significant relationship between stakeholder engagement and sustainability (r = 0.796, p < 0.01), with regression results confirming that stakeholder engagement significantly influences sustainability (β = 0.167, p = 0.002). However, the study also established that stakeholder engagement remains largely superficial, with limited inclusion of marginalized groups such as small-scale fishers, women, youth, and persons with disabilities. This exclusion undermines trust, reduces compliance, and weakens the legitimacy of marine governance systems. The study concludes that while stakeholder engagement is critical for the sustainability of the blue economy, its effectiveness depends on inclusivity, transparency, and institutional support. It recommends strengthening inclusive governance frameworks, enhancing institutional coordination, and promoting capacity building to improve stakeholder engagement and the sustainability of Kenya’s blue economy.

title: Forecast-Assisted Deep Reinforcement Learning for Energy Management of Hydrogen-Enabled Community Microgrids
summary: Hydrogen-enabled community microgrids can improve renewable energy utilization and local resilience, but their operation is complicated by uncertain residential demand, variable renewable generation, dynamic electricity prices, and the coup
content: Hydrogen-enabled community microgrids can improve renewable energy utilization and local resilience, but their operation is complicated by uncertain residential demand, variable renewable generation, dynamic electricity prices, and the coupled dynamics of battery and hydrogen storage. This paper extends a previously developed proximal policy optimization (PPO) energy management system by adding multi-horizon community-load forecasts to the controller state. The framework is evaluated for a 1,000-household residential microgrid in Rockhampton, Australia. Forecast accuracy is mixed: the 1-h model achieves an RMSE of 239.32 kW and an R2 of 0.201, whereas the 6-h and 12-h horizons produce negative R2 values; the 24-h forecast achieves an RMSE of 249.79 kW, a MAPE of 62.52%, and an R2 of 0.126. Despite this limited predictive accuracy, the forecast-enriched PPO converges approximately 14.3% earlier than the non-predictive controller and increases the final reward by 8.3%. Annual savings rise from A$2,439.86 without forecasts to A$2,765.83 with forecasts, an incremental gain of A$325.97 (13.4%), while renewable utilization increases from 35.3% to 36.4%. Grid imports fall to 58,147.49 kWh. Resilience tests show a 20.1% battery protection value during grid outages, but no measurable forecast-specific resilience improvement. The results demonstrate that even imperfect forecasts can improve learning and economic dispatch while also showing that forecast calibration, common test conditions, and longer-duration outage studies are necessary before broader deployment claims can be made.

title: Unlocking the grid flexibility potential of fifth-generation district heating and cooling systems through user-level demand-side strategies
summary: The increasing penetration of renewable energy sources is intensifying the need for energy flexibility solutions capable of supporting power grid stability. In this context, fifth-generation district heating and cooling (5GDHC) systems repr
content: The increasing penetration of renewable energy sources is intensifying the need for energy flexibility solutions capable of supporting power grid stability. In this context, fifth-generation district heating and cooling (5GDHC) systems represent a promising yet still underexplored interface between urban thermal demand and electricity grids. This work investigates the potential of 5GDHC systems to provide energy flexibility services through demand-side management strategies implemented at building-user level. A physics-based dynamic modelling framework is developed, integrating building thermal demand calculation, heat pump performance modelling, and the representation of thermal energy storage and electrical batteries. Flexibility-oriented control strategies, including indoor temperature setpoint modulation, battery-assisted heat pump operation, and thermal energy storage integration, are simulated and assessed using dedicated flexibility indices for downward and upward load modulation and load shifting. The methodology is applied to a multi-user 5GDHC case study considering three alternative thermal balancing configurations: ground-coupled, groundwater-based, and solar-assisted solutions. The results of the simulative case study show that setpoint modulation enables short-term flexibility, achieving electricity load reductions of up to 37% and load increases of up to 26%. Battery integration enhances flexibility further, enabling load variations of 51–60%, while thermal energy storage achieves the highest performance, with load modulation exceeding 99% and load shifting fractions up to 54%. Flexibility provision is accompanied by primary energy savings of up to 11% and operating cost reductions of up to 14%, with groundwater-based configurations yielding the best overall performance. The proposed framework provides a robust tool to support the design and operation of flexible, low-carbon district energy systems.

title: Optimization and OGY-based chaos control of a bistable piezoelectric energy harvester for enhanced power generation
summary: This study investigates the nonlinear dynamics and energy-harvesting performance of a bistable piezoelectric energy harvester. The work was motivated by the need to improve the power output and dynamic predictability of piezoelectric harves
content: This study investigates the nonlinear dynamics and energy-harvesting performance of a bistable piezoelectric energy harvester. The work was motivated by the need to improve the power output and dynamic predictability of piezoelectric harvesters operating under nonlinear and potentially chaotic conditions. Numerical simulations were performed using the STONEHENGE software, and systematic parameter scans were conducted to examine the system response under different excitation and coupling conditions. Instead of treating the excitation amplitude and frequency as directly controllable design variables, the analysis was used to identify how the harvester responds over a representative range of operating conditions and how its performance can be improved through suitable physical and nonlinear system parameters. A Python-based optimization algorithm was then implemented to evaluate the parameter combinations associated with improved energy-harvesting performance within the simulated parameter domain. The revised analysis therefore focuses on performance trends, nonlinear coupling effects, and control-oriented stabilization rather than reporting specific excitation conditions as practical design targets. The results showed that the nonlinear coupling coefficient β plays a decisive role in determining energy-harvesting efficiency, indicating that nonlinear coupling can be exploited to enhance power generation. Within the investigated numerical framework, the optimized response reached a maximum power output of 69.052 mW, demonstrating the potential benefit of parameter-guided nonlinear tuning. In addition, the Ott-Grebogi-Yorke control method was applied to suppress chaotic oscillations and stabilize the system into a periodic regime. This transition from chaotic to periodic motion improved the predictability of the generated electrical response. The findings demonstrate that optimized bistable piezoelectric systems, combined with chaos-control strategies, offer a promising route for efficient and reliable vibration-based energy harvesting.

title: Estimated hourly electricity demand profiles for each county in the contiguous United States
summary: In this data descriptor, we present hourly electricity demand estimates for each county in the contiguous United States from 2016 to 2023. The demand profiles represent the sum of two components for each county. The first is the weighted av
content: In this data descriptor, we present hourly electricity demand estimates for each county in the contiguous United States from 2016 to 2023. The demand profiles represent the sum of two components for each county. The first is the weighted average of reported hourly demand profiles for North American Electric Reliability Corporation balancing authority (BA) regions and subregions, scaled to match annual estimates of county-level retail sales and direct use of electricity and weighted by the estimated percentage of county load served by each BA region or subregion. The second is the weighted average of modeled hourly, county- and sector-level distributed photovoltaic (DPV) capacity factor profiles, scaled to match annual estimates of on-site consumption of DPV-generated electricity for each county and weighted by the percentage of consumption attributable to each sector.

title: Analysis and Performance of an Enhanced Inverter with Third-Harmonic Injected PWM Technique
summary: Abstract Multilevel inverters are widely used in high and medium power systems owing to their ability to generate a high-quality output with less stress on the devices and improved efficiency. However, the traditional multilevel inverter co
content: Abstract Multilevel inverters are widely used in high and medium power systems owing to their ability to generate a high-quality output with less stress on the devices and improved efficiency. However, the traditional multilevel inverter configurations are associated with an increased number of switches, complex control and uneven voltage stress distribution. The purpose of this study is to design a proposed 9-level multilevel inverter that can be expanded to higher levels by cascading the basic modules. The proposed topology, when controlled using the third-harmonic injected pulse width modulation (THI-PWM) technique achieves improved DC bus utilization and minimize harmonic distortion. The proposed inverter is compared with various other topologies and investigated the performance of the proposed inverter through simulation and hardware results. The proposed one has high conversion efficiency, minimum voltage stress on the power switches and efficient harmonic suppression. The output voltage and current waveforms satisfy the IEEE 519 harmonic standards and the consistency between the simulation and hardware results confirms the validity and reliability of the proposed system.

title: Offshore wind and wave energy on the European Atlantic shelf: A multi-decadal high-resolution metocean analysis
summary: There is a significant difference between theoretical offshore renewable energy (ORE) resource assessments and actual net energy yield considering device technical specifications and logistical weather window constraints. This study conduct
content: There is a significant difference between theoretical offshore renewable energy (ORE) resource assessments and actual net energy yield considering device technical specifications and logistical weather window constraints. This study conducts a high-resolution geospatial assessment of Western European waters using 30 years of hourly metocean data from the new ECHOWAVE hindcast dataset. Logistical weather windows have been modelled to penalise the raw technical resource of commercial-scale ORE device specifications to get a more realistic picture of the net energy yield. Scenarios have considered the IEA 15MW reference wind turbine and a 20MW wave energy cluster for energy production. For operations, a CTV (Crew Transfer Vessel) and SOV (Service Operation Vessel) for have been considered separately and compared. While raw wind energy yield peaks in the Atlantic, net yield is maximized in the more sheltered and accessible Irish Sea and North Sea when a CTV is considered. However, transitioning to an SOV strategy effectively rehabilitates the Atlantic resource by lifting annual operational accessibility to 60–70 %. Wave energy also faces a steep logistical penalty dictated by the choice of maintenance strategy: under CTV constraints, net energy yield drops by roughly 44 % from gross peaks, though the highest net-yielding zones expand eastward from the Atlantic core resource. Conversely, utilising SOVs substantially mitigates these accessibility constraints, demonstrating that advanced logistics represent an absolute baseline necessity for utility-scale wave viability. 30-year historical metocean peaks have also been mapped in this study, identifying extreme significant wave heights exceeding 20 m and wind speeds over 40 m/s in the North Atlantic. The findings highlight how high-resolution metocean datasets such as ECHOWAVE can provide highly valuable information for site selection and planning of commercial ORE projects, as the sector scales up over the coming decades.

title: Efektivitas Koagulan Alami Serbuk Kulit Pisang Kepok (Musa Paradisiaca L) Terhadap Kekeruhan Air Sungai
source: Indonesian Journal of Innovation Multidisipliner Research
summary: Air sungai banyak dimanfaatkan masyarakat untuk kebutuhan sehari-hari, namun sering memiliki tingkat kekeruhan tinggi sehingga memerlukan pengolahan sebelum digunakan. Salah satu alternatif pengolahan ramah lingkungan adalah penggunaan koag
content: Air sungai banyak dimanfaatkan masyarakat untuk kebutuhan sehari-hari, namun sering memiliki tingkat kekeruhan tinggi sehingga memerlukan pengolahan sebelum digunakan. Salah satu alternatif pengolahan ramah lingkungan adalah penggunaan koagulan alami dari serbuk kulit pisang kepok (Musa paradisiaca L.) yang mengandung pektin, tanin, dan saponin. Pemanfaatan limbah kulit pisang kepok sebagai koagulan alami diharapkan dapat menjadi solusi yang lebih ekonomis, mudah diperoleh, serta mengurangi ketergantungan terhadap koagulan kimia yang berpotensi menimbulkan dampak negatif bagi lingkungan. Penelitian ini bertujuan mengetahui efektivitas serbuk kulit pisang kepok terhadap penurunan kekeruhan air Sungai Martapura serta menentukan dosis optimum yang paling efektif. Jenis penelitian yang digunakan adalah true experimental dengan desain post test only with control. Variasi dosis yang digunakan yaitu 50 mg/L, 100 mg/L, 150 mg/L, 200 mg/L, dan 250 mg/L dengan 4 kali pengulangan serta satu kelompok kontrol. Parameter yang diperiksa meliputi tingkat kekeruhan dan pH air setelah perlakuan. Pengukuran tingkat kekeruhan dilakukan menggunakan turbidimeter, sedangkan pengukuran pH menggunakan pH meter sesuai prosedur laboratorium. Analisis data dilakukan menggunakan uji One Way Anova. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan seluruh variasi dosis mampu menurunkan tingkat kekeruhan dibandingkan kelompok kontrol dengan rerata kekeruhan awal 43,6 NTU. Penurunan terbaik diperoleh pada dosis 150 mg/L dengan rerata kekeruhan 30,8 NTU. Hasil uji One Way Anova menunjukkan terdapat perbedaan signifikan antar perlakuan terhadap penurunan kekeruhan air (p<0,05). Temuan ini menunjukkan bahwa kandungan senyawa aktif pada serbuk kulit pisang kepok berperan dalam proses koagulasi dan flokulasi sehingga mampu membantu mengurangi partikel penyebab kekeruhan di dalam air. Serbuk kulit pisang kepok mampu menurunkan kekeruhan air sungai, namun belum memenuhi baku mutu air bersih <3 NTU sehingga masih diperlukan pengolahan lanjutan agar mendapatkan hasil yang optimal.

title: Influence of Landscape Maintenance on Users’ Experiences in Tourist Centres
summary: The diligent upkeep of landscapes in tourist centres is crucial not only for aesthetic reasons but also for fostering a sense of safety and security, ensuring a positive experience for visitors and preventing the degradation of the park env
content: The diligent upkeep of landscapes in tourist centres is crucial not only for aesthetic reasons but also for fostering a sense of safety and security, ensuring a positive experience for visitors and preventing the degradation of the park environment. This study evaluates the influence of landscape maintenance on user experiences in selected tourist sites across Southwest Nigeria. This study employed primary and secondary data. Descriptive statistics, including percentages and index, were used. Six tourist centres were chosen, one from every state in southwest Nigeria. Of the 2,520 tourists to the tourist centres, 345 tourists (13.7%) were chosen by the accidental sampling technique, out of which 317 responses from respondents were received and analysed. The results show that users were generally satisfied with the cleanliness and maintenance of the elements. Specifically, with an average Users’ Satisfaction of Maintenance Indices (USMI) of 4.20. The results obtained show strong satisfaction with the cleanliness of tourist centres, with 4.34, while satisfaction with the regular upkeep and maintenance of landscape elements was 4.15. Maintenance of vegetation (trees, shrubs, and lawns) had 4.07, maintenance of lighting had 4.47, and maintenance of signage and information boards had 4.21. When considering the impact of landscape maintenance predictors on user satisfaction, the coefficient values of the multiple regression equivalences showed that the maintenance of water features (ponds, fountains, and streams) had the most significant impact on users’ satisfaction with β = 0.362, p < 0.00. The study shows that landscape maintenance has consequences on users’ experience in tourist centres.

title: The International Energy Architecture and Energy Transition
summary: Chapter 5 is written by Volker Roeben and is titled “The International Energy Architecture and Energy Transition.” The author starts by highlighting the energy need, generally, and then underscoring the current transition from coal and oil
content: Chapter 5 is written by Volker Roeben and is titled “The International Energy Architecture and Energy Transition.” The author starts by highlighting the energy need, generally, and then underscoring the current transition from coal and oil to new kinds of energy, in particular. In this analysis, the author highlights the crux of the matter, namely, the climate protection policies in shaping the next generation energy architecture. This started with the UN Sustainable Development Goals (primarily Goal 7) and the UN Climate Change Framework (predominantly the Paris Agreement), but has received an elevation following the ICJ&s;s Climate Change Advisory Opinion from 2025. This chapter expertly navigates the climate protection policies as they intersect with more traditional energy architecture; that is, customary rules, the Energy Charter Treaty, the WTO, and international investment law. In order to better understand the landscape around energy law, the author outlines the policy work of key institutional actors – such as the International Energy Agency, the International Renewable Energy Agency, the International Atomic Agency, the Energy Charter Conference, the WTO, and so on. The chapter also illustrates the role played by ‘non-State actors’ as interlocutors of the architectural framework. Finally, even though focused on the framework of international energy system design, the author explains that the ‘energy-related law of dispute resolution and settlement also is part of this system, and hence it absorbs this impetus’.

title: Barnyard millet (Echinochloa species): an underutilized nutritional powerhouse with emerging nutraceutical benefits
summary: The impact of climate change presents an opportunity for orphan crops like millet to contribute to sustainable food systems. A prime example of an orphan crop with special traits and the potential to develop climate-smart agriculture is Bar
content: The impact of climate change presents an opportunity for orphan crops like millet to contribute to sustainable food systems. A prime example of an orphan crop with special traits and the potential to develop climate-smart agriculture is Barnyard millet (BYM). Alkaloids, steroids, polysaccharides, glycosides, tannins, phenols, dietary lignans and flavonoids are just a few of the antioxidants that are abundant in BYM. BYM’s antioxidant potential, prebiotic status, anti-inflammatory, hypoglycemic, antibacterial and anticancerous properties help it to combat a myriad of diseases. The antinutritional compounds present in BYM such phytic acid, tannins, polyphenols, and amylase inhibitors limit the absorption of minerals because they form complexes with dietary minerals like calcium, zinc, magnesium, and iron and make them inaccessible for absorption. Various processing methods like dehulling, soaking, heating, gamma irradiation, cold plasma processing, fermentation might enhance the nutritional and technological functional qualities of BYM. The bioactives in BYM can improve their bioavailability, in vitro digestibility, efficiency, structural modification and stability by biological processing techniques such as germination and fermentation employing microbial strains. BYM straw’s high cellulose and hemicellulose percentage makes C5 and C6 sugars accessible for bioconversion into bioethanol.

title: Photocatalytic Degradation of Methylene Blue and Methyl Orange Using Aloe Vera-Modified TiO? Under UV and Solar Irradiation
source: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
summary: This study investigates the photocatalytic degradation of two organic dyes, Methylene Blue (MB) and Methyl Orange (MO), using aloe vera-modified titanium dioxide (TiO<sub>2</sub>) as a photocatalyst under both UV and solar irradiation. The
content: This study investigates the photocatalytic degradation of two organic dyes, Methylene Blue (MB) and Methyl Orange (MO), using aloe vera-modified titanium dioxide (TiO<sub>2</sub>) as a photocatalyst under both UV and solar irradiation. The modification of TiO<sub>2</sub> with aloe vera extract through high-temperature calcination at 850°C for 2 hours was employed to enhance photocatalytic activity. Experimental results demonstrated that 0.75 g of modified TiO<sub>2</sub> achieved the highest degradation efficiencies: 91% for MB and 75% for MO under sunlight exposure for 1 hour. The study also compared the performance of TiO<sub>2</sub> and TiO<sub>2</sub>/ZnO composites applied as paste coatings on beaker walls, which showed reduced efficiency (45-55% for MB, 27-34% for MO) due to light shielding effects. These findings align with established literature on TiO<sub>2</sub>-based photocatalysis and demonstrate the potential of bio-modified photocatalysts for sustainable wastewater treatment applications. The degradation followed pseudo-first-order kinetics, with optimal performance observed at higher catalyst concentrations and direct catalyst-dye contact.

title: Locational Marginal Pricing in Electricity Markets: A Methodological Framework for Economic Efficiency
summary: This paper presents a methodology to determine Locational Marginal Prices (LMPs) in electricity markets by integrating DC optimal power flow (DC-OPF) with loss factor modeling based on system distribution factors. The proposed framework com
content: This paper presents a methodology to determine Locational Marginal Prices (LMPs) in electricity markets by integrating DC optimal power flow (DC-OPF) with loss factor modeling based on system distribution factors. The proposed framework combines detailed AC power flow simulations in DIgSILENT PowerFactory, used to calculate total system losses, with an optimization model implemented in Pyomo to capture the effects of transmission and generation constraints as well as marginal losses. Two DC-OPF models are formulated as follows: Model 1 without losses and Model 2 including loss factors derived from AC analysis. Results obtained for a simplified three-node system and the IEEE 39-node benchmark demonstrate that, under unconstrained conditions, LMPs converge to a uniform value, whereas transmission congestion introduces price differentials consistent with theoretical expectations. Incorporating marginal losses refines the pricing signals, ensuring a more accurate representation of real system operations. The proposed approach enhances computational efficiency while improving economic transparency, offering a robust tool for market operators and regulators to design and validate nodal pricing mechanisms.

title: Workforce Development for Sustainable Built Environments: A Systematic Review of Skills Gaps, Training Deficiencies, and Strategic Pathways in the Green Construction Industry
source: Journal of Geography Environment and Earth Science International
summary: This systematic review examines workforce development challenges linked to the transition towards sustainable built environments. The review focuses on skills gaps, training deficiencies, and strategic pathways in the green construction ind
content: This systematic review examines workforce development challenges linked to the transition towards sustainable built environments. The review focuses on skills gaps, training deficiencies, and strategic pathways in the green construction industry, where sustainability targets increasingly require competencies in energy efficiency, smart building systems, renewable energy integration, digital construction and green certification. A structured literature search was conducted across academic databases, government sources, and industry repositories to identify publications from 2022 to 2025. Thirty-four sources were selected using defined inclusion criteria and analysed thematically in relation to workforce shortages, competency requirements, training approaches, access barriers and policy responses. The synthesis indicates that the development of the green construction workforce is constrained by both quantitative labour shortages and qualitative skills gaps. The most prominent gaps relate to system integration, energy performance assessment, green building certification, digital construction technologies and renewable energy systems. Training barriers include cost, geographical inequality, fragmented curricula and limited institutional capacity to update programmes in response to technological change. Evidence from the reviewed literature suggests that coordinated action is required across vocational education, specialist certification, industry-academia partnerships, digital and immersive training approaches, continuous professional development, and inclusive recruitment. The review concludes that sustainable built-environment delivery depends on integrated workforce planning that links policy requirements, training systems, and industry demand.

title: Modified Cascaded H-Bridge 5-Level Inverter for Improved Power Quality and Reduced Harmonic Distortion
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Multilevel inverters have become an essential technology in modern power electronics due to their ability to produce high-quality output voltage with reduced harmonic distortion and lower switching losses. Among various multilevel inverter
content: Multilevel inverters have become an essential technology in modern power electronics due to their ability to produce high-quality output voltage with reduced harmonic distortion and lower switching losses. Among various multilevel inverter topologies, the Cascaded H-Bridge (CHB) inverter has gained considerable attention because of its modular structure, simple control strategy, and excellent voltage quality. This paper presents a Modified Cascaded H-Bridge 5-Level Inverter designed to improve output waveform quality while reducing the Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) and component count compared with conventional topologies. The proposed inverter utilizes an optimized switching strategy to generate five distinct voltage levels (+Vdc, +Vdc/2, 0, –Vdc/2, and –Vdc), resulting in a staircase waveform that closely approximates a sinusoidal output. The system is modeled and analyzed using MATLAB/Simulink to evaluate its steady-state performance under different loading conditions. Performance parameters such as output voltage, output current, inverter efficiency, switching losses, THD, and voltage regulation are investigated. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed modified topology significantly improves power quality, enhances system efficiency, and minimizes harmonic distortion while maintaining a simple and cost-effective design. The modular architecture also enables easy scalability for medium- and highpower applications. The proposed inverter is suitable for renewable energy systems, industrial motor drives, uninterrupted power supplies (UPS), electric vehicle power converters, and smart grid applications where reliable and efficient power conversion is required.

title: DSP control and ESP32-based monitoring interface for a 1kW isolated Ćuk converter for photovoltaic applications
summary: This study presents the design, modelling and experimental validation of a 1kW isolated dc-dc Ćuk converter like a solution designed for residential photovoltaics (PV) applications, emphasizing the importance of proper energy management and
content: This study presents the design, modelling and experimental validation of a 1kW isolated dc-dc Ćuk converter like a solution designed for residential photovoltaics (PV) applications, emphasizing the importance of proper energy management and operational flexibility. The examined converter supports both grid-connected and off-grid operating scenarios, designed to function at power levels suitable for standard residential loads. The research presents typical operational scenarios, like varying load demand and variable energy production from renewable sources. System-level modeling and performance evaluation are realised to validate the converter's suitability for residential application. Simulation-based validation is conducted in the CASPOC environment to evaluate voltage and current behavior across critical components, confirming theoretical design assumptions. A digital control and monitoring framework is implemented using a DSP-based control platform combined with an ESP32-enabled communication interface, enabling remote monitoring via a CAN-to-Wi-Fi gateway and a dedicated graphical user interface. Experimental testing demonstrates stable operation, proper voltage regulation, and compatibility with PV-to-battery energy transfer scenarios. The research indicates that the proposed converter structure provides an attractive option for residential solar systems, improving operational flexibility and efficiency. The study highlights power electronics as an essential enabling technology for developing robust and environmentally friendly household energy infrastructures, focusing on isolated operation and interoperability with energy storage in both grid-connected and off-grid contexts.

title: Environmental justice and social vulnerability in climate governance: legal and institutional responses to inequality in developing societies
summary: Climate change and ecological decline serve as core societal crises, revealing stark disparities in how environmental hazards and resources are shared. This study investigates the intersection of environmental policy, social vulnerability,
content: Climate change and ecological decline serve as core societal crises, revealing stark disparities in how environmental hazards and resources are shared. This study investigates the intersection of environmental policy, social vulnerability, and justice. It particularly highlights emerging nations, where marginalized groups disproportionately endure ecological dangers. Using a multidisciplinary and socio-legal framework, the research evaluates how current environmental regulations and institutional designs succeed or stumble in mitigating climate-driven social impacts. It contends that environmental rules must transcend mere regulatory compliance. Instead, they should integrate core values of fairness, transparency, and the defense of vulnerable demographics. The paper examines the capacity of public policies, legal systems, and grassroots involvement to drive inclusive environmental sustainability aligned with the Sustainable Development Goals, primarily SDGs 10, 13, and 16. By proving that environmental fairness is a fundamental matter of governance, inequality, and human advancement rather than an isolated ecological issue, this study substantially enriches wider dialogues on societal transformation

title: MLP artificial neural network model for predicting natural gas composition variability
source: Chemical and Process Engineering New Frontiers
summary: This paper proposes an artificial neural network model, MLP 17-37-5, to predict the share of five natural gas components (methane, ethane, propane, nitrogen, and carbon dioxide) in the natural gas mixture in a pipeline network, depending on
content: This paper proposes an artificial neural network model, MLP 17-37-5, to predict the share of five natural gas components (methane, ethane, propane, nitrogen, and carbon dioxide) in the natural gas mixture in a pipeline network, depending on selected calendar and weather factors. Natural gas composition variability in the pipeline network results from supplying it with gas of varying composition and from different suppliers. Using statistical analysis of 35,064 actual measurement data sets, factors (modelinput data) significantly affecting gas composition variability were selected. Models differing in structure (the MLP 17-37-5 model or five MLP 17-37-1 models) and the number of neurons in the hidden layer (from 20 to 230 neurons) were trained using sets ranging from 8,760 to 35,064 actual data points obtained using the chromatographic method. The quality of the models was assessed based on the correlation coefficient, while the quality of the forecasts was assessed based on the nRMSE error of the forecasts obtained for a new data set of 8,760 data points. The MLP 17-37-5 model was shown to predict natural gas composition with an average error of nRMSE = 0.321. The article proposes a ready-made tool, which has no equivalent in the literature, allowing for a significant reduction in the number of chromatographic tests performed to determine the composition of natural gas. This is a completely new approach to studying changes in the composition of natural gas over time, which in the proposed forecasting model depend on selected factors (not analyzed in chromatographic studies).

title: GENDERED ENERGY INSECURITY: ADRESSING THE NEXUS BETWEEN ENERGY SECURITY RISKS AND GENDER EQUALITY
source: Çukurova Üniversitesi Sosyal Bilimler Enstitüsü Dergisi
summary: Energy is widely recognized as a fundamental driver of economic growth and sustainable development. However, uncertainties in energy supply and demand pose significant challenges to global energy security. This study investigates whether ge
content: Energy is widely recognized as a fundamental driver of economic growth and sustainable development. However, uncertainties in energy supply and demand pose significant challenges to global energy security. This study investigates whether gender equality can mitigate energy security risks by examining the case of the United States over the period 1989–2019. Using an Autoregressive Distributed Lag (ARDL) framework, the study explores the long-run relationship between gender equality (SDG 5) and energy security (SDG 7), measured by the Gender Inequality Index (GII) and the Energy Security Risk Index (ESRI), respectively. The analysis also incorporates key control variables, including real GDP per capita, urban population, and the share of female investors. The findings provide evidence of a significant long-term relationship between gender equality and energy security risk. By integrating gender dynamics into the analysis of energy security, this study contributes to the literature by offering a more comprehensive perspective and provides policy-relevant insights for promoting inclusive and resilient energy systems.

title: Design and Implementation of a New Non‐Isolated High Step‐Up DC–DC Converter With Two Switches and Voltage Stress Reduction
source: International Journal of Circuit Theory and Applications
summary: ABSTRACT This paper presents a novel non‐isolated high step‐up DC–DC converter featuring two power switches with reduced voltage stress. The proposed topology achieves a high voltage gain without employing transformers or coupled inductors,
content: ABSTRACT This paper presents a novel non‐isolated high step‐up DC–DC converter featuring two power switches with reduced voltage stress. The proposed topology achieves a high voltage gain without employing transformers or coupled inductors, making it suitable for renewable energy systems and electric vehicle applications. Two distinct switching strategies, namely complementary switching and simultaneous switching, are investigated to enhance voltage gain over different duty‐cycle ranges. By optimally combining these two strategies, the converter attains high voltage gain, reduced semiconductor stress, and improved efficiency across a wide operating range. A comprehensive theoretical analysis, including steady‐state operation and loss evaluation, is conducted. The performance of the proposed converter is validated through simulations and experimental results obtained from a 200 W laboratory prototype. The experimental results demonstrate a maximum efficiency of 96.4%, confirming the effectiveness, reliability, and practical applicability of the proposed converter.

title: A decomposition method for optimizing the operation of power-to-X energy systems with detailed process models
summary: The growing reliance on renewable energy necessitates extending energy systems with complex processes such as power-to-X. Due to the diverse operational characteristics of these processes, the corresponding optimization problems are highly
content: The growing reliance on renewable energy necessitates extending energy systems with complex processes such as power-to-X. Due to the diverse operational characteristics of these processes, the corresponding optimization problems are highly complex and result in models that are computationally difficult to solve. To address this computational challenge, this work proposes a decomposition method to solve operational optimization problems for complex energy systems with detailed process models. The method decomposes the original optimization problem into optimization problems with different levels of model granularity by incorporating a surrogate model for each process. Building on prior work focusing on a single continuous process system, this method is expanded to handle multiple and more complex process systems. To this end, we introduce a surrogate modeling approach for multistage process systems and develop three solution approaches for the operational optimization problems. The method is applied to minimize the daily operational cost of a power-to-X energy system with detailed process models of a PEM electrolyzer, a direct air capture plant and two methanation processes. All three solution approaches yield comparable operational costs, but differ in computational efficiency. The most efficient solution approach identifies an optimal operational strategy in under one hour. Additionally, a sensitivity study evaluates the impact of key parameters on the performance of the method, demonstrating its robustness and adaptability. The results highlight the potential of the proposed method to efficiently optimize the operations of complex energy systems with detailed process models.

title: Design and Thermodynamic Modeling of a Recuperative ORC Binary System for Double Flasher Geothermal Power Plant
summary: This research evaluates the thermodynamic performance of a recuperative binary Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC) integrated with a double-flash geothermal power plant, modeled using Aspen HYSYS for medium-enthalpy resources (200°C) common in Indo
content: This research evaluates the thermodynamic performance of a recuperative binary Organic Rankine Cycle (ORC) integrated with a double-flash geothermal power plant, modeled using Aspen HYSYS for medium-enthalpy resources (200°C) common in Indonesia, such as Lahendong or Wayang Windu fields. Configurations compared include standalone double-flash (baseline), double-flash + simple ORC, and double-flash + recuperative ORC, with n-pentane selected as the optimal working fluid for its superior net power output, thermal efficiency, and low specific investment cost among alternatives like isopentane and isobutane. Fixed geothermal brine inputs (180°C, 15 bar, ~144-146 kg/s) simulate real Indonesian conditions. Results demonstrate the recuperative design's superiority: ORC efficiency rises by ~2% (13.71% vs. 11.71%), overall plant efficiency by 3.26% (21.5% vs. 18.24%), and net power output by 168% (5229 kW vs. 1514.6 kW baseline), driven by recuperator-enabled heat recovery that cuts evaporator duty by 15-25% and condenser rejection. Geothermal segment efficiency improves to 5.62% from 4.55%. Recuperator design features shell-and-tube units (e.g., 5181 mm tube length, 2100 mm shell diameter, U=65 W/m²K, area ~1889 m²) with minimal pressure drops.
